docs.title: AIRelays Docs
docs.text:
AIRelays is a local OpenAI-shaped relay with provider-scoped runtimes.

  • OpenAI runtime: ChatGPT subscription access with multi-account balancing, plus image generation and edits (gpt-image-2)
  • Claude runtime: chat, completions and Responses with images, files, conversations and tool calls, balanced across AIRelays-owned claude CLI subscription profiles, separate from your personal Claude Code sign-in

Generated through AIRelays with POST /v1/images/generations; the request is in API Notes.

Install the headless relay and CLI (macOS, Linux):

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lpalbou/AIRelays/main/scripts/install-headless.sh | bash

Install the desktop tray app (macOS Apple Silicon, Linux x86_64):

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lpalbou/AIRelays/main/scripts/install-desktop.sh | bash

On Windows (x64), run irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lpalbou/AIRelays/main/scripts/install-desktop.ps1 | iex in PowerShell. See the repository README for details.

docs.title: Traffic log retention API
docs.text:
GET /v1/relay/logging returns current policy and disk usage without deleting logs. PUT /v1/relay/logging validates, persists and applies a partial policy update immediately; omitted fields retain their saved values. These routes use the same bearer-token gate and rate limits as the other /v1/* routes.

Example PUT body (all values must be integers; sizes are MiB):

{"retention_days": 30, "max_total_mb": 1024, "max_file_mb": 50}

Both responses contain policy, policy_source (saved or config, including built-in defaults), policy_path, logs_dir, usage_bytes, file_count, over_budget, cleanup_interval_seconds, last_cleanup_at, deleted_files, deleted_bytes, oversized_records, dropped_records, and last_error. Cleanup counters and errors are local to the process answering the request; disk usage and saved policy are shared. last_cleanup_at is the most recent completed cleanup pass, which may have encountered deletion errors. It is null before a pass completes.

Invalid values, unknown fields, zero size limits, or a file limit larger than the total budget return 422 without altering the saved policy. Storage failures preventing policy reads or persistence return 503. A successfully saved policy returns 200 even if cleanup fails; inspect last_error and over_budget before reporting successful reclamation. A policy update permanently deletes eligible old files. GET requests do not trigger reclamation.

Defaults: 7 days, 1024 MiB total, 50 MiB per file. retention_days: 0 removes the age limit but leaves size enforcement enabled. See configuration for bounds, precedence, rotation behavior, migration, and CLI/tray controls.

For a side-by-side summary of what works on GPT models and on Claude models, see Capabilities.

docs.title: Compatibility Adaptations (read this first)
docs.text:
The verified upstream is the ChatGPT subscription backend, not the public platform API. AIRelays adapts requests on the three text-generation routes (/v1/responses, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions) rather than letting them fail. Parameter stripping is always disclosed; other compatibility normalizations are documented here and may log dedicated adaptation records when the request shape itself is repaired:

  • Removed unsupported parameters: temperature, top_p, presence_penalty, and frequency_penalty are stripped before the upstream call because the upstream rejects them ("Unsupported parameter: temperature"). Caller-supplied end-user identifiers (user, safety_identifier) are also stripped because the verified subscription backend does not honor them, as is seed (best-effort determinism in OpenAI's own API; neither upstream supports it). The names of removed parameters are returned in the x-airelays-ignored-parameters response header and logged as a compatibility_adaptation traffic record with the reason. Generation runs with the upstream's own defaults. The same adaptation applies on the Claude routes: the local claude CLI exposes no sampling controls, so these parameters are stripped and disclosed there too instead of failing the request.
  • Output-token limits: max_completion_tokens (preferred) and max_tokens on chat and completions, and max_output_tokens on /v1/responses, are honoured on both runtimes. GPT models receive them as the upstream's max_output_tokens, which enforces them (values below 16 get the upstream's own 400). On Claude models each CLI model call is capped and the run stops when the first one reaches the limit, before the CLI would continue on its own. A cut answer reports finish_reason: "length" (status: "incomplete" on /v1/responses).
  • Unrecognized parameters: on /v1/chat/completions and /v1/completions (both runtimes), a parameter AIRelays does not recognize is dropped and listed in x-airelays-ignored-parameters like the stripped ones, so nothing is ignored silently. This covers cache hints such as prompt_cache_retention; on Claude models it also covers verbosity, prompt_cache_key, metadata and service_tier. A parameter sent as null means "not set" and is not listed. Names are percent-encoded in the header (so any JSON key is a valid header value) and the list is capped at about 2 KB, ending in ,... when cut; the traffic log keeps every name. /v1/responses forwards unrecognized parameters to the upstream as-is.
  • Verbosity and prompt caching: on OpenAI models, chat verbosity is forwarded as the Responses text.verbosity, and prompt_cache_key is forwarded as-is.
  • Reasoning effort: reasoning_effort (chat completions and completions) and reasoning.effort (responses) are forwarded verbatim to OpenAI models; on claude:* models reasoning_effort maps to the local CLI's --effort flag on both text routes. An explicit JSON null is treated as absent. Each model's supported modes and default are published in /v1/models under airelays.reasoning. Unsupported Claude values are rejected with the supported list (the CLI would silently ignore them); unsupported OpenAI values surface the upstream's own error. Modes and defaults come from the provider catalog when available and vary by model. Omitting effort leaves the choice to the provider; Claude can use an adaptive default. An empty Claude modes list means no effort parameter is advertised for that model.
  • Structured outputs: response_format.type=json_schema is forwarded (translated) to OpenAI models. With strict: true, the schema is rewritten to OpenAI's strict-mode form: every property becomes required, optional ones accept null, and additionalProperties defaults to false (a schema that sets it to anything else is rejected). Without strict: true the schema is forwarded unchanged with strict: false, OpenAI's default, sent explicitly because the upstream otherwise assumes strict mode. The same applies to text.format on /v1/responses. response_format.type=json_object is forwarded as the upstream's native JSON mode (text.format: {"type": "json_object"}), with OpenAI's rule that the messages must mention JSON enforced by the upstream. In JSON mode, chat system and developer messages are sent as developer input messages rather than instructions, so a system prompt that mentions JSON counts, as on OpenAI. On claude:* chat completions both json_schema and json_object are honored via the claude CLI's native --json-schema enforcement. Supported types per model are published in /v1/models under airelays.structured_output.
  • Cursor chat-route compatibility: AIRelays accepts two malformed request families currently observed from Cursor custom OpenAI endpoints on /v1/chat/completions: full Responses-style bodies (input, instructions, flat tools, etc.) and flat Responses-style custom tool definitions / tool choices / assistant tool calls (for example the ApplyPatch tool). AIRelays normalizes those requests locally, sends the canonical Responses shape upstream, and translates upstream custom_tool_call items back into chat-completions tool_calls on both streaming and non-streaming responses. Mixed-shape requests that contain both messages and input, or tool outputs that do not reference a preceding assistant tool call in the same request (or, with conversation, an earlier turn), are rejected loudly.
  • Rejected loudly instead of adapted: store=true, n>1, best_of/echo/logprobs/suffix on /v1/completions, and on both chat and completions (both runtimes) a non-empty stop, a true logprobs, a nonzero top_logprobs, or a non-empty logit_bias. Neither upstream can honor them and dropping them would change the output, so they return a clear 422 error. Chat web_search_options, moderation, audio, prediction and non-text modalities are rejected the same way; for the first four any non-null value counts, since web_search_options: {} means "search with defaults". Default values (null, false, 0, empty, best_of: 1, modalities: ["text"]) are accepted on both runtimes; on /v1/completions, an integer logprobs (including 0) is a request.
  • Image generation: /v1/images/generations and /v1/images/edits forward only what the subscription's image service applies (verified live): prompt, model, background and moderation; quality and size are forwarded too, but the service picks its own. The service does not validate the rest, so AIRelays checks every parameter against OpenAI's published values first (422 with the offending param), produces n images with n upstream calls, answers stream: true with one completed event per image, and lists the parameters it dropped (output_format, output_compression, partial_images, response_format, style, user, safety_identifier, input_fidelity), plus quality and size whenever the rendered image differs from the request, in x-airelays-ignored-parameters with a compatibility_adaptation record. A mask is refused (422). See POST /v1/images/....
  • OpenAI model admission: when AIRelays can fetch the live ChatGPT Codex model catalog for the authenticated OpenAI account(s), OpenAI requests are forwarded only for model ids that appear in that catalog or in [providers.openai].extra_models. Other ids are rejected locally with 404 model_not_found and suggestions from /v1/models, instead of failing later upstream with an account-scoped unsupported-model error. In multi-account mode, the same cache is invalidated when the enrolled OpenAI account set changes, so admission follows the union of their catalogs. Routing and failover use only the accounts listing the model, even when all supporting accounts are cooling down. Explicit unlisted extra_models overrides remain eligible across the pool; if an override appears in an account catalog, its discovered subset takes precedence.
  • Account affinity: with multiple OpenAI accounts, a conversation is pinned to the account that served its first turn (protects upstream prompt caching); failover to another account happens only at turn boundaries, logged as an account_failover traffic record.
  • Upstream failures and automatic retry: failed OpenAI calls are retried automatically with exponential backoff (retry_attempts, default 3 retries waiting 5s/20s/60s; each retry re-runs account failover) while no response byte has reached the client — non-streaming requests and the pre-header phase of streaming ones. On final failure the client gets OpenAI-shaped error JSON ({"error": {...}}) with the real HTTP status: the upstream's own code (e.g. server_is_overloaded) and, for quota errors, resets_in_seconds. After a stream has started, failures surface as an in-band data: {"error": ...} event (chat/completions) or a verbatim response.failed/error event (responses passthrough); mid-stream failures are not retried. Retries are logged as retry_backoff traffic records (retry_skipped explains deliberate non-retries), and upstream failure events as upstream_stream_error records.

docs.title: GET /v1/models
docs.text:
Returns an OpenAI-style models list built from the enabled provider runtimes.

  • OpenAI models come from the authenticated ChatGPT/Codex upstream catalog. The default client version setting, auto, follows the installed codex --version, with a tested version floor when the CLI is missing or older. Model names are not hard-coded into automatic discovery.
  • Claude models come from the installed CLI's initialization catalog, including its alias resolutions and per-model reasoning modes. Discovery sends no generation prompt. Both claude:* aliases and discovered concrete claude-* ids are accepted. No Claude models are listed until an AIRelays Claude account is connected.
  • models starting with claude: or claude- route to the Claude runtime when it is enabled
  • other model ids route to the OpenAI runtime when it is enabled
  • Each model record includes an airelays extension block with provider identity, route capabilities, a reasoning block (parameter, supported modes, default), and a structured_output block (parameter, supported types for response_format on chat completions).
  • Provider catalogs are cached in memory for models_cache_ttl_seconds seconds. The default is 300 seconds; 0 disables the cache.
  • Cached OpenAI model lists are scoped to the current local OpenAI auth account and ignored after logout or account changes.
  • GET /v1/models?refresh=true bypasses the provider catalog caches, including all OpenAI account catalogs. The desktop Refresh button uses this parameter, and the open Models tab also reloads every five minutes while the relay is reachable.
  • airelays.discovery_source identifies upstream_catalog, claude_cli, or a configured override. airelays.upstream_model is the selector forwarded upstream. airelays.resolved_model reports the concrete Claude model when the CLI supplies it; airelays.display_name carries its provider label. Aliases keep following the CLI's selection; use a concrete id to pin a model version.
  • Configured OpenAI extra_models and Claude models extend discovery. They are retained for compatibility and may not have catalog confirmation. A missing or incompatible Claude CLI retains configured ids and the last successful catalog; providers.claude.models_discovery_error in relay status reports discovery failures. Failed Claude probes are cached for the same interval to avoid repeatedly launching a failing CLI.
  • With several OpenAI accounts, discovery returns the union of successful catalogs and preserves each model's metadata. airelays.account_availability reports supported and total account counts without disclosing account identities. A failed account catalog does not hide models returned by other accounts. Routing retains last-known membership during catalog outages rather than broadening a known subset.
  • airelays.catalog_visibility and airelays.description preserve upstream metadata. Entries marked hide appear as upstream-hidden in the desktop; AIRelays does not infer their underlying identity or promote them as recommended models.
  • Catalog discovery reports provider availability and capabilities; it does not generate a test response for every model. Account limits and upstream availability still apply when serving a request.

GET /v1/models/{model} returns that model's entry from the list (ids match case-insensitively, as for requests), or 404 model_not_found. While the OpenAI catalog cannot be fetched, OpenAI ids return the catalog error instead.

docs.title: GET /v1/subscription/status
docs.text:
Returns a normalized subscription-usage snapshot with per-window usage percentages, window labels ("5h", "weekly", derived from each window's duration), and reset times. Which windows appear is plan-dependent upstream policy; only reported windows are returned.

  • default provider is OpenAI (source: chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage)
  • ?provider=claude returns Claude subscription usage in the same normalized shape (see Subscription Status)
  • ?account=<email-or-prefix> selects one enrolled OpenAI account
  • ?provider=claude&account=<email-or-id> selects one Claude account; the setup-token account (default) returns 422 unsupported_for_provider because Claude reports no usage for setup tokens
  • ?all_accounts=true returns the list shape with one entry per enrolled OpenAI account (an entry carries an error instead of a status when that account's usage probe fails)
  • ?raw=true includes the raw upstream payload (OpenAI only)
  • rate_limits.image_generation reports the image-generation quota, a separate 24-hour upstream bucket the usage endpoint does not include: the same window fields, plus source (image_response or probe), observed_at, and relay (the images this relay made in the window). See Subscription Status
  • ?provider=claude&all_accounts=true returns {"object": "subscription_status_list", "provider": "claude", "accounts": [...]}, keyed by stable account slug. Each entry has slug, email, and one of status, error, or usage_unsupported (the setup-token account); a failed reading affects only its entry
  • Claude readings come from each profile's Claude Code (get_usage). A reading without live data keeps the last good values with stale: true, its age, and stale_reason (usage_unavailable, nonessential_traffic_disabled, cli_unsupported, cli_failed). Without any good reading, the account reports an error message instead of numbers

GET /v1/account/rate_limits is an alias.

docs.title: POST /v1/relay/accounts/refresh
docs.text:
Re-checks every enrolled OpenAI account's capacity immediately and returns the refreshed account list. Releases are evidence-gated: an account's usage-limit hold is lifted only when its fresh usage report shows capacity, so live traffic can never slip onto a still-exhausted account during the re-check. Use it when you know an account has recovered and don't want to wait for the scheduled reset. CLI equivalent: airelays accounts refresh.

With ?provider=claude, refreshes Claude account usage while respecting each account's cached readings and persisted backoff.

docs.title: GET /v1/relay/accounts/resets
docs.text:
Lists each enrolled OpenAI account's usage-limit reset credits: the resets Codex offers under Redeem reset (for example the "Full reset" OpenAI grants to Codex users), read from the same subscription at chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/rate-limit-reset-credits. Nothing is inferred: every fact comes from the upstream listing and the account's usage report. CLI equivalent: airelays accounts resets.

  • ?account=<email-or-prefix> selects one account (slug also accepted)
  • ?force=true bypasses the one-minute cache shared with usage probes
  • ?raw=true includes the raw upstream listing per account
{
  "object": "accounts.resets",
  "available_count": 1,
  "accounts": [
    {
      "slug": "default",
      "email": "you@example.com",
      "resets": {
        "object": "rate_limit_reset_credits",
        "captured_at": "2026-10-18T09:12:03Z",
        "available_count": 1,
        "applicable_available_count": 0,
        "redeemable_now": false,
        "total_earned_count": 0,
        "next_expiry_at": "2026-11-07T00:00:05Z",
        "credits": [
          {
            "id": "RateLimitResetCredit_…",
            "reset_type": "codex_rate_limits",
            "status": "available",
            "supported_by_plan": true,
            "title": "Full reset",
            "description": "…",
            "granted_by": "Codex Team",
            "granted_at": "2026-10-08T00:00:05Z",
            "expires_at": "2026-11-07T00:00:05Z",
            "expires_in_seconds": 1712282,
            "expired": false,
            "redeem_started_at": null,
            "redeemed_at": null
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  ]
}

available_count is how many credits the account holds; applicable_available_count (from the usage report) is how many the upstream would apply right now. A credit held while usage is below its limit is available but not applicable: redeemable_now is false, and redeeming it answers nothing_to_reset without spending it. An account whose listing cannot be read carries an error string instead of resets.

docs.title: POST /v1/relay/accounts/resets/redeem
docs.text:
Redeems one reset credit now, through AIRelays, without opening an OpenAI app: the call Codex makes behind Yes, use reset (chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/rate-limit-reset-credits/consume). The relay then re-reads that account's usage so a lifted limit returns it to rotation immediately. Irreversible on OpenAI's side; the desktop and the CLI (airelays accounts redeem <email>) ask for confirmation first.

Body (JSON, all fields optional with one enrolled account):

  • account: email, unambiguous prefix, or slug; required when several accounts are enrolled (the relay never picks one for you)
  • credit_id: redeem this specific credit; otherwise the upstream chooses
  • redeem_request_id: idempotency key forwarded to the upstream; a retry with the same key cannot spend a second credit (generated when omitted)
{
  "object": "accounts.reset_redeem",
  "slug": "default",
  "email": "you@example.com",
  "outcome": "reset",
  "known_outcome": true,
  "reset_applied": true,
  "windows_reset": 2,
  "credit_id": "RateLimitResetCredit_…",
  "redeem_request_id": "6d1f…",
  "status": { "object": "subscription_status", "…": "fresh usage after the redeem" }
}

outcome is the upstream's code verbatim: reset (applied; windows_reset says how many windows restarted), nothing_to_reset (usage did not need a reset; credit kept), no_credit, or already_redeemed. reset_applied is true only for reset. status is null when the follow-up usage read fails. Errors: 400 when several accounts are enrolled and none is named, 404 unknown account, 409 ambiguous prefix, 422 malformed field; upstream rejections pass through with their status.

docs.title: GET /v1/relay/status
docs.text:
Returns relay diagnostics, provider readiness, provider cache status, and requests_total — the count of real (non-monitoring) requests served by this process, usable as a lightweight activity signal. OpenAI model-list cache diagnostics live under providers.openai.models_cache.

providers.claude.accounts lists AIRelays-owned Claude accounts with their slug, email, readiness, managed_profile, oauth_token_source, request cooldown, and unavailable_models (models the account cannot serve right now although its sign-in works, with seconds until AIRelays tries them again). managed_profile is false only for the setup-token account; oauth_token_source is profile or file. providers.claude.balance reports their selection strategy. A second ready profile of the same subscription carries duplicate_of and is counted once; an account whose identity differs from its enrollment is not eligible.

providers.openai.accounts[] (or providers.openai itself with a single account) carries image_usage: the image-generation quota as last read and the relay's own image count for the window; image_limited and image_limited_for_seconds appear while an account's image bucket is benched (text requests are unaffected).

GET /v1/relay/status?activity_only=true returns only {"requests_total": N}. It requires the same authentication as the full status, but it does not scan storage or probe providers, is not itself counted, and does not consume rate-limit quota or a concurrency slot, so clients such as the desktop tray can poll it frequently.

docs.title: CLI Diagnostics
docs.text:
airelays usage prints every usage window the running relay reports, per account and provider, text windows and the image-generation quota alike (--json for the raw payloads).

airelays status reports local config, relay-token, and provider readiness state. airelays doctor runs the same local checks and also probes the OpenAI upstream /models route plus a tiny /responses smoke request when the OpenAI runtime is enabled and logged in, and reports a CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN set in the relay's environment, which AIRelays ignores. Use airelays doctor --skip-response to skip the response smoke request. airelays models lists every model id the running relay accepts, grouped by provider (--json supported). airelays accounts resets shows each OpenAI account's usage resets and airelays accounts redeem <email> spends one through the running relay (see the two /v1/relay/accounts/resets routes above; --yes skips the confirmation, --credit <id> picks a credit).

docs.title: POST /v1/responses
docs.text:
OpenAI runtime:

  • general OpenAI Responses envelope
  • stream=true|false
  • local conversations
  • local files and verified input_file forms

Current OpenAI limits:

  • store=true rejected
  • output-token limits enforced upstream (see Compatibility Adaptations)

Claude runtime:

  • the same request and response shapes, streamed (response.created, response.output_text.delta, function_call items, response.completed) or not, translated to the Claude runtime's chat path: input (text, input_image, input_file, function_call and function_call_output items), instructions, function tools, tool_choice, text.format (json_schema, json_object) and reasoning.effort
  • conversation works as on GPT models; previous_response_id, store: true, background: true and stored prompts are refused (Claude models keep no responses: use conversation)
  • log probabilities (top_logprobs, or message.output_text.logprobs in include) are refused; other include values and text.verbosity are dropped and listed in x-airelays-ignored-parameters
  • a function_call_output is a string or text parts; image and file parts in tool outputs are refused (as in role: "tool" messages on chat completions)
  • function tools run non-strict, since Claude has no strict tool mode (strict: true is listed in x-airelays-ignored-parameters). Server-side tools (web search, file search) are not available on Claude models
  • other unsupported fields, such as reasoning.summary, are dropped and listed in x-airelays-ignored-parameters

docs.title: POST /v1/chat/completions
docs.text:
OpenAI runtime:

  • current AIRelays OpenAI compatibility path
  • standard chat-completions messages requests supported
  • Responses-shaped request bodies also accepted on this route for Cursor compatibility and translated back to chat-completions responses
  • tool support includes both OpenAI function tools and custom tools; AIRelays also accepts Cursor's flatter Responses-style custom tool shape on this route
  • tool_choice accepts auto, none, required, a named function or custom tool, and allowed_tools
  • function tools run non-strict unless function.strict is true, as in OpenAI's chat API; AIRelays sends strict: false explicitly because the upstream otherwise assumes strict. strict must be a boolean here and in response_format.json_schema
  • assistant messages may carry content: null alongside tool_calls or a refusal, as OpenAI SDKs send them back
  • the deprecated functions/function_call interface is supported end to end: replies carry message.function_call (streamed as delta.function_call) with finish_reason: "function_call", one call per reply, and role: "function" messages answer the matching call by name. Send either tools or functions, not both, and use tools with conversation
  • file content parts use OpenAI's shape, {"type": "file", "file": {...}}, with a local file_id from POST /v1/files or inline file_data plus filename

Claude runtime:

  • discovered Claude aliases and concrete model ids, plus configured overrides
  • system, developer, user, assistant and tool messages
  • stream=true|false
  • images (image_url: a PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP data URL, an http(s) URL, or a local file_id) and documents (file parts: PDF or UTF-8 text, as file_data or a local file_id), in any user message; an image or document Claude cannot read returns 422, never a silently degraded answer. detail has no Claude equivalent
  • function tools: Claude decides which of the client's tools to call, and the calls come back as OpenAI tool_calls with finish_reason: "tool_calls"; the client runs its tools and sends the results back as tool messages, as with GPT models. AIRelays never runs a tool: the CLI's built-in tools are off, the client's tools are only descriptions behind a helper that executes nothing, every call is denied before execution, and the run stops at the call. The CLI's startup report is checked on every request, and a request stops if any tool appears that AIRelays did not define (see Tool calls on Claude models). Refused with 422 because Claude cannot honour them: a forced call (tool_choice required or a named tool), parallel_tool_calls: false, non-function tools, and parameters that are not an object schema. strict: true tools run non-strict, listed in x-airelays-ignored-parameters (Claude has no strict tool mode). A request whose tools the CLI could not load fails with 502 cli_tools_unavailable instead of answering without them; the /no-tools/ routes refuse tools as on GPT models
  • conversation works as on GPT models
  • no audio
  • reasoning_effort supported (low, medium, high, xhigh, max), mapped to the CLI's --effort flag; omitted means the model's adaptive default
  • structured outputs supported: response_format.type=json_schema maps to the CLI's --json-schema flag (native schema enforcement). The response content is the enforced JSON only — a run that produces no schema-conforming output fails loudly instead of returning prose. On streaming requests the JSON text streams as the content deltas. Enforcement runs as an internal tool turn upstream, so schema-enforced calls bill some additional output tokens. Unsupported response_format shapes (including a missing type) are rejected with a 422; serialized schemas are capped at 200 KB (they travel on the local CLI's argv). Two documented leniencies versus OpenAI: json_schema.name is optional (metadata the CLI does not use), and strict is ignored because the CLI's native enforcement is always strict — clients can only get stricter behavior than asked, never weaker. json_object asks the model, in the system prompt, for a single JSON object and checks the answer before returning it (a surrounding code fence is removed); an answer that is not one JSON object returns 502 invalid_json_output and does not pause any account. An answer cut short (finish_reason: "length") or refused (content_filter) is returned as is. In JSON mode a streamed answer arrives as one content chunk, because it is checked first.
  • every Claude request carries a system prompt: the client's, or a minimal one when the client sends none, so the Claude CLI's own built-in agent prompt never applies.
  • sampling parameters stripped and disclosed via x-airelays-ignored-parameters (the claude CLI has no sampling controls); other unsupported generation controls rejected locally
  • with no AIRelays Claude account connected, claude:* requests (here and on /v1/completions) return 503 provider_auth_error: "No Claude account is connected to AIRelays. Run airelays claude login or airelays claude set-token."

docs.title: POST /v1/images/generations and POST /v1/images/edits
docs.text:
OpenAI's Images API on the ChatGPT subscription runtime (GPT models only; claude:* models return 422 unsupported_for_provider). The subscription serves the GPT image model; /v1/models lists it as gpt-image-2 and the routes accept any gpt-image-* id (the upstream does not report which model answered). Other ids return 404 model_not_found.

  • prompt (required, up to 32,000 characters), model (default gpt-image-2), background (transparent, opaque, auto) and moderation (low, auto) are forwarded; background is applied (verified live, transparent images carry an alpha channel).
  • quality (auto, low, medium, high) and size (auto, or WIDTHxHEIGHT with both sides multiples of 16, an aspect ratio between 1:3 and 3:1, a longest edge up to 3840 and 655,360 to 8,294,400 pixels) are checked and forwarded, but the service decides on its own: observed live, flat-shape prompts came back 1254x1254 at low whatever was asked (portrait, square, landscape, low, medium or high), and photographic prompts 1536x1024 at medium. The response's size and quality report what was rendered, and whenever they differ from the request the parameter is listed in x-airelays-ignored-parameters. Values outside OpenAI's sets are refused with 422 naming the field in param (verified live: an unknown quality renders at low, any model is accepted, an impossible size is replaced).
  • n (1 to 10) runs one upstream call per image, up to three at a time, and merges the images and usage into one response; one failed image fails the request, as on OpenAI.
  • stream: true answers text/event-stream with one image_generation.completed (edits: image_edit.completed) event per image in OpenAI's event shape, once the images exist. There are no partial images, so partial_images is listed as ignored. Failures surface as real HTTP statuses, never as an empty stream.
  • the answer is OpenAI's ImagesResponse: created, data[].b64_json, background, output_format (png), quality, size, usage (input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens with image/text details). size is the rendered resolution, which may differ from the request. Each image also carries the upstream's generation_id.
  • output_format, output_compression, partial_images, response_format: "url", style, user and safety_identifier are accepted, checked, dropped and listed in x-airelays-ignored-parameters: the upstream returns PNG b64_json whatever they say. Unknown parameters are dropped and listed the same way; null values are not listed.
  • edits take OpenAI's multipart form (image or image[] files, PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 16 and 20 MiB each, plus text fields) or a JSON body whose image is a data URL, a local file_id from /v1/files, or an array of them. input_fidelity is listed as ignored (the model always uses high fidelity). mask is refused with 422: the upstream edits whole images and dropping the mask would change the output.
  • an image call waits up to [providers.openai] image_timeout_seconds (default 300). Quota rejections (429 usage_limit_reached) carry Retry-After; with several accounts the request fails over to one whose image quota is open (the image bucket is benched separately from the text windows), and automatic retry applies as on the text routes.
  • the traffic log keeps request and response shapes with image sizes, never the image bytes; upstream_usage records carry the image quota reading.
curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/images/generations \
  -H 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_AIRELAYS_TOKEN' \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt": "a watercolor fox", "size": "1024x1024", "quality": "low"}' \
  | python3 -c 'import base64,json,sys; open("fox.png","wb").write(base64.b64decode(json.load(sys.stdin)["data"][0]["b64_json"]))'

curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/images/edits \
  -H 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_AIRELAYS_TOKEN' \
  -F image=@fox.png -F prompt='make the fox blue'

With the OpenAI SDK, client.images.generate(model="gpt-image-2", prompt=...) and client.images.edit(model="gpt-image-2", image=open("fox.png", "rb"), prompt=...) work as documented; client.images.generate(..., stream=True) yields image_generation.completed events.

docs.title: POST /v1/completions
docs.text:
OpenAI runtime:

  • current AIRelays OpenAI compatibility path

Claude runtime:

  • discovered Claude aliases and concrete model ids, plus configured overrides
  • text prompt in, text out (images, documents and tools are on /v1/chat/completions and /v1/responses)
  • stream=true|false
  • reasoning_effort supported (same modes and mapping as chat completions)
  • response_format rejected loudly (not part of the completions API; ignoring it would silently hand unenforced text to a client that asked for JSON — use /v1/chat/completions for structured outputs)
  • sampling parameters stripped and disclosed via x-airelays-ignored-parameters; other unsupported generation controls rejected locally

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Every error uses OpenAI's error object, with a detail copy of the message for existing AIRelays clients:

{"error": {"message": "...", "type": "invalid_request_error", "param": null, "code": "model_not_found"}, "detail": "..."}
  • type is invalid_request_error for client errors, rate_limit_error for 429 and server_error for 5xx (authentication problems with the upstream subscription use authentication_error)
  • unknown models return 404 with code model_not_found; unsupported parameters and features return 422 (see ADR 0001)
  • a Claude answer in json_object mode that is not one JSON object returns 502 invalid_json_output; retrying usually helps, or use json_schema
  • a quota or cooldown rejection returns 429 with a Retry-After header when the reset time is known (OpenAI SDKs then wait, or stop retrying when the reset is more than two minutes away); a Claude CLI that is not signed in returns 503, not 401, because the client's own credentials are fine
  • every response carries an x-request-id header, the id AIRelays uses in its traffic log; OpenAI SDKs expose it as request_id
  • Claude streams start only once the CLI produces output, so failures before the first token are real HTTP errors; failures after it arrive in-band as data: {"error": {...}} without [DONE]

docs.title: Finish reasons and refusals
docs.text: finish_reason is stop, length, tool_calls, content_filter, or function_call for requests using the deprecated functions. An upstream response cut short by its token limit reports length, and one stopped by the provider's content filter (OpenAI) or a refusal (Claude) reports content_filter. OpenAI refusals are returned in message.refusal (streamed as delta.refusal). Chat responses always include choices[].logprobs and message.refusal, null when not applicable.

docs.title: Token usage on chat and completions
docs.text:
/v1/chat/completions and /v1/completions report usage in OpenAI's Chat Completions shape on both runtimes:

{
  "prompt_tokens": 18,
  "completion_tokens": 5,
  "total_tokens": 23,
  "prompt_tokens_details": {"cached_tokens": 4, "cache_write_tokens": 2},
  "completion_tokens_details": {"reasoning_tokens": 1}
}
  • prompt_tokens counts every prompt token, cached ones included; prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens and cache_write_tokens break out the tokens read from and written to the prompt cache (cache_write_tokens is typed in recent openai-python releases; older SDKs keep it as an extra field). total_tokens is prompt_tokens + completion_tokens.
  • the details objects and their members appear only when the provider reports them (the Claude runtime has no completion_tokens_details)
  • when a provider reports no readable usage, usage is omitted rather than filled with zeros
  • streaming: with stream_options: {"include_usage": true}, every chunk carries "usage": null, and one extra chunk with "choices": [] and the usage follows the chunk with finish_reason, before data: [DONE]. Without it, chunks have no usage field. A stream that fails sends no usage chunk.
  • /v1/responses returns the Responses API usage (input_tokens, output_tokens, ...) unchanged
  • stream_options sent without stream: true has no effect; it is dropped and listed in x-airelays-ignored-parameters
  • for the OpenAI runtime, traffic logs keep the upstream usage as reported (upstream_usage and outbound_usage records). For Claude, the raw CLI result is logged for non-streaming requests (provider_response) and stream lines only when stream-line logging is enabled; Claude outbound_usage records carry the translated usage

docs.title: POST /v1/files
docs.text:
Local AIRelays file storage for the OpenAI runtime compatibility path.

  • purpose is a multipart form field, as OpenAI SDKs send it: one of assistants (the default when omitted), batch, fine-tune, vision, user_data or evals
  • GET /v1/files supports OpenAI's after, limit (1 to 10000, default 10000), order (desc by default) and purpose query parameters and returns first_id, last_id and has_more, so SDK auto-pagination works, including loops that delete each file as they go (a deleted file still anchors after for a day)
  • expires_after is not supported and returns 422; delete files explicitly
  • GET /v1/files/{file_id}, GET /v1/files/{file_id}/content and DELETE /v1/files/{file_id} complete the set

docs.title: POST /v1/conversations
docs.text:
Local AIRelays conversation storage for the OpenAI runtime compatibility path.

  • create a conversation, optionally with initial items (Responses input items) and metadata; GET, POST (metadata update) and DELETE /v1/conversations/{id} manage it
  • pass its id as conversation on /v1/responses (a string or {"id": ...}), /v1/chat/completions or /v1/completions. The conversation's items are prepended to each turn's input, and once a turn succeeds its input and output items are appended, as in OpenAI's conversations. A failed turn leaves the conversation unchanged
  • stored output items are the replayable ones: assistant messages, every call the client answers (items with a call_id, such as function, custom and local shell calls), and reasoning items that carry encrypted_content (request it with include: ["reasoning.encrypted_content"]). Other reasoning items and server-side tool calls are not kept; their outcome is in the messages that follow
  • local files are stored as file_id references and inlined on every turn. Initial items are checked like a turn's input (the file exists and fits its content part). Deleting a file that a conversation uses makes its later turns fail with 422; start a new conversation
  • the conversation items API (/v1/conversations/{id}/items) is not available and returns 501
  • on /v1/chat/completions, a tool message may answer a tool call made in an earlier turn of the conversation

Conversations work on Claude models too (chat completions and /v1/responses), and one conversation can continue across models and runtimes. Claude cannot replay other models' reasoning items, so they are skipped on Claude turns, and a conversation holding GPT custom tool calls cannot continue on a Claude model (422).

docs.title: Tool calls on Claude models
docs.text:
The claude CLI is an agent that would normally run tools itself. AIRelays uses it so that Claude only decides which tool to call, and the client runs it, exactly as with OpenAI:

Safeguard What it does Built-in tools off The CLI starts with no shell, file, web or agent tools. Descriptions only The client's tools reach the CLI through a helper inside AIRelays that lists them and answers every call with "not executed"; it can run nothing. Startup check Every request checks the CLI's own list of available tools; anything AIRelays did not define stops the request. Pre-execution deny The CLI asks a check before running any tool, and the answer is always "deny". Stop at the call The run is interrupted as soon as Claude has made its calls.

The first two make running a tool impossible; the other three add defence in depth. The CLI itself still starts its usual helper programs on every Claude request (a read-only git check of its empty working folder, ps, ioreg and, on macOS, the keychain reader for its sign-in).

docs.title: Unsupported Routes
docs.text:
These currently return 501 unsupported_error. Every 501 AIRelays returns carries x-should-retry: false, so OpenAI SDKs do not retry it:

  • embeddings
  • image variations (/v1/images/variations); generations and edits are served, see above
  • audio
  • realtime sessions

Claude models are also rejected on any route that is not part of their published subset.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
AIRelays is an OpenAI-shaped edge over provider-specific local runtimes.

  • The default runtime uses the ChatGPT Codex subscription backend and balances requests across every enrolled OpenAI account with capacity.
  • The Claude account pool selects an AIRelays-owned CLI profile for each local claude -p subprocess. Claude Code owns authentication and token refresh; the personal Claude Code sign-in is never used.
flowchart LR
    Client["OpenAI-compatible client"] -->|"bearer token"| Edge

    subgraph Relay["AIRelays (local)"]
        Edge["FastAPI edge\nauth · rate limits · traffic log"] --> Registry["Provider registry\nmodel id → runtime"]
        Registry -->|"other model ids"| Retry["Retry layer\nexponential backoff\npre-first-byte only"]
        Retry --> Pool["OpenAI account pool\nbalanced selection · benching · failover"]
        Registry -->|"claude:* model ids"| ClaudePool["Claude account pool\ncapacity · cooldown · failover"]
        ClaudePool --> ClaudeRT["Claude runtime per account\nvalidation · isolated environment"]
        Pool --> B1["Backend adapter\naccount 1"]
        Pool --> B2["Backend adapter\naccount N"]
    end

    B1 --> Upstream["ChatGPT subscription backend"]
    B2 --> Upstream
    ClaudeRT --> CLI["local claude CLI\n(claude -p subprocess)"]
    CLI --> Anthropic["Selected Claude subscription"]

docs.title: Request Flow
docs.text:
1. FastAPI receives an OpenAI-shaped request.
  2. Middleware enforces relay auth and local abuse controls.
  3. AIRelays resolves the request model id to a provider runtime. OpenAI model admission uses the account-scoped upstream catalog; catalog requests follow the installed Codex version in automatic mode. Claude refreshes the installed CLI's initialization catalog on demand and registers its aliases and concrete model ids before resolving requests. Catalogs use a bounded cache, with an explicit refresh path shared by the API and desktop Models page. Discovery does not submit inference prompts.
  4. Images and documents are checked the same way for both runtimes before any upstream call. The OpenAI runtime uses the shared request/response transforms plus the OpenAI backend adapter. Claude requests from every route go through one entry point: /v1/responses bodies are translated to the chat shape and back, conversation history is attached, uploaded files are inlined, and the Claude runtime turns the conversation into the single message one CLI run receives (see Claude Request Path).
  5. On the OpenAI runtime, the account pool picks the account: conversation affinity first, then — among accounts with capacity that serve the requested model — the one with the most remaining quota in its longest usage window (balance = "balanced", the default), strict rotation ("round_robin"), or the first such account ("ordered"). Which usage windows an account reports is plan-dependent, so the pool ranks windows by duration and balances on the longest (weekly) budget — the scarce one — while short-window exhaustion is handled by benching and failover. Accounts already benched (a usage probe or an earlier request showed their window is spent) are skipped outright, so requests route straight to accounts with capacity. Account-scoped failures (usage limits, in-stream failure events, dead credentials, transport errors) bench the account until it recovers and fail over to the next one — only before any content byte reaches the client; on streams, events that precede content are buffered so this guarantee holds.
  6. If every account fails, the retry layer waits an exponential backoff (retry_attempts, default 3 retries at 5s/20s/60s) and re-runs the whole pool pass — again only while no response byte has reached the client. Quota errors whose reset lies beyond the backoff budget return immediately.
  7. The selected runtime returns streamed or aggregated output in the matching OpenAI-shaped envelope; failures return OpenAI-shaped error JSON with the upstream's own reason, and failures after streaming started surface in-band.
  8. AIRelays logs the request, runtime selection, account selection, retries, and result.

Claude selection uses available account slots, fresh weekly usage, and known model-specific limits. Without fresh usage, eligible accounts rotate. A CLI authentication, quota, or transient failure puts the account into cooldown; the pool can try another eligible account before any response bytes are sent. Each Claude request is one fresh CLI run; conversation history, when a client uses conversation, is kept by AIRelays and sent with each turn, so there is no account affinity across turns.

docs.title: Claude Request Path
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    Chat["/v1/chat/completions"] --> Entry
    Resp["/v1/responses"] -->|"Responses ↔ chat translation"| Entry
    Entry["Claude entry point\nconversation history · uploaded files inlined"] --> Prep["Request preparation\nimage and document check · transcript blocks\ntool definitions · output limit"]
    Prep --> Pool["Claude account pool"]
    Pool --> Run["One CLI run per request\nstream-json input and output"]
    Run -->|"client tools as descriptions"| Stub["Tool helper\nlists tools, runs nothing"]
    Run -->|"before any tool runs"| Guard["Pre-execution check\nalways deny"]
    Run -->|"tool calls made or output limit reached"| Stop["Run interrupted\ncalls or partial answer returned"]

Each Claude request is one CLI run that receives the whole conversation as a single user message, with images and documents in place, so a turn is one model call. Built-in CLI tools are off; the client's function tools reach the CLI only as descriptions served by a helper that executes nothing, every call is denied before execution, and the run stops as soon as Claude has made its calls. The CLI's own report of available tools is checked on every request. See Tool calls on Claude models and Capabilities.

airelay.claude_auth owns enrollment metadata under data_dir/claude/accounts/<id>/account.json. Each adjacent config/ directory is owned by Claude Code and stays at a stable path because macOS credentials are scoped to it. The optional setup token (data_dir/claude-token) is the inference-only account default, run from its own relay-owned data_dir/claude/token/config. The ambient Claude Code sign-in, an inherited CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN are not accounts. airelay.claude_accounts owns selection and failover; ClaudeCliRuntime owns per-profile execution, model discovery, and usage backoff.

Usage readings come from the profile's own CLI through the Claude Code SDK get_usage control request, at startup and every five minutes; AIRelays never reads Claude credentials. Claude Code renews the profile's token while answering, which keeps idle profiles signed in. A reading without live data keeps the last good one, marked stale, and failures back off up to 60 minutes, persisted across restarts. Every Claude Code process gets an explicit environment, its profile's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and a relay-owned working directory, and is ended gracefully (stdin closed or SIGTERM before SIGKILL). See the profile decision and relay-owned accounts.

flowchart LR
    Pool["Claude account pool\nselection · cooldown · failover"]
    Pool --> Profile["Browser profile runtime\nCLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR: claude/accounts/ID/config"]
    Pool --> Token["Setup-token runtime (default)\nCLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR: claude/token/config"]
    Profile -->|"claude -p (requests)"| CLI1["claude CLI\nprofile credentials"]
    Refresh["Usage refresh\nstartup · every 5 min"] -->|"get_usage control request\n(no prompt)"| CLI1
    CLI1 -->|"renews OAuth token\nlive limits"| Refresh
    Token -->|"claude -p (requests)"| CLI2["claude CLI\ninference only"]
    CLI1 --> Anthropic["Claude subscription"]
    CLI2 --> Anthropic

The personal Claude Code sign-in (~/.claude) is not part of this picture: AIRelays never reads it, routes through it, or signs it out.

docs.title: OpenAI Account Pool Lifecycle
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Probing: relay starts (2+ accounts)
    Probing --> Serving: usage + model catalogs fetched
    Serving --> Benched: usage limit / dead credentials / transport failure
    Benched --> Serving: window reset reached, or a fresh usage probe shows capacity
    note right of Benched
        Releases are evidence-gated:
        only a usage snapshot newer than
        the bench can lift it early.
    end note

At launch, a multi-account pool probes each account's usage and model catalog in the background, so accounts already at their limit are benched and model-aware balancing works from the first request.

The public OpenAI model catalog is the union across enrolled accounts. Selection, affinity, and every failover attempt are restricted to the requested model's supporting subset, never to an unsupported account as a last resort. Per-account catalogs are also refreshed before routing when their TTL expires. Catalog failures retain last-known routing membership; they do not establish support on an unknown account.

docs.title: Capabilities by Account Type
docs.text:
AIRelays serves GPT models (your ChatGPT subscription) and Claude models (your Claude subscription) through one OpenAI-compatible endpoint, http://127.0.0.1:8317/v1, with the same API key. The model name picks the account type: gpt-… models use the ChatGPT runtime, claude:… and claude-… models use the Claude runtime. /v1/models lists both, with each model's capabilities under airelays.capabilities.

This page is the reference for what works on each account type. Details for each route are in API Notes.

Legend: ✅ supported · ⚠️ accepted but not applied, and listed in the x-airelays-ignored-parameters response header · ❌ refused with a clear error (422, or 501 for whole endpoints).

docs.title: Streaming notes
docs.text:
Both account types stream answers as they are generated. Three parts arrive whole instead:

  • each tool call's arguments arrive in one chunk;
  • on Claude models, a JSON-mode answer arrives in one chunk, because it is checked before it is sent;
  • on Claude models, the first token takes a few seconds while the local CLI starts.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
AIRelays resolves settings in this order:

  1. CLI flags
  2. AIRELAYS_* environment variables
  3. legacy OPENAI_ENDPOINT_* migration variables where supported
  4. ~/.config/airelays/config.toml
  5. built-in defaults

Traffic-log retention is live configuration: a saved policy in the selected log directory takes precedence over its [logging] defaults. See Traffic log retention below.

docs.title: Traffic log retention
docs.text:
Traffic logs rotate hourly and at a size limit. Cleanup runs on startup, every 60 seconds while the relay is running (including when idle), on rotation, and when applying a policy. Both age and size limits apply; whichever requires removing a file first wins. Defaults are deliberately bounded on upgrades too.

Parameter Default Meaning retention_days 7 Maximum age since a file's last write; 30 means 30 days, 0 disables only the age limit. Range: 0–36500. max_total_mb 1024 Total managed traffic-log budget in MiB (1 GiB by default). Range: 1–1048576. max_file_mb 50 Rotate before the next record would exceed this size in MiB. Range: 1–10240; must not exceed the total budget.

Retention is an upper limit, not a promise of seven days of history: under load, the disk budget removes older files sooner. Cleanup reserves room for the active file, so usage can be below the configured budget by up to a chunk plus the last whole file removed. Files are deleted whole, oldest modification time first. The budget counts file contents; filesystem allocation and metadata overhead are not included in usage_bytes.

From the CLI (also works with the relay stopped):

airelays logs                         # policy and current usage; no cleanup
airelays logs --retention-days 30      # keep up to a month, save and apply
airelays logs --retention-days 7 --max-total-mb 1024 --max-file-mb 50
airelays logs --json                  # machine-readable policy, usage, errors
airelays logs --config /path/to/config.toml --retention-days 14

The selected --config, --data-dir, and --logs-dir determine which log directory is managed. Use the same directory as the running relay.

In the cross-platform tray app, open Settings → Traffic log retention. Choose 1 week, 1 month (30 days), or a custom duration and disk limit, then Apply log retention. The relay must be running for the tray controls; the CLI can configure it offline. This section applies independently of the other settings' Save & Restart workflow. It shows disk usage and cleanup errors.

The HTTP API exposes the same policy. API/tray updates apply immediately. Other relay processes sharing the directory pick up the saved policy on their next write or within 60 seconds while idle.

Policy changes are saved atomically to <logs_dir>/.retention.json. That file overrides the three TOML retention defaults and survives restarts, CLI sessions, and the tray's regeneration of config.toml. Change it through the API or CLI; editing the TOML defaults after saving a policy does not override that policy. The stream_lines option remains a separate startup setting.

Cleanup includes existing YYYY/MM/DD-HH.log files and new size-rotated YYYY/MM/DD-HH.<uuid>.log files. It does not manage console/stdout logs, uploads, conversations, unrelated files, symlinks, or hard links. Use an app-owned local log directory; every writer sharing it must run a retention-aware AIRelays version. External writers or an older relay can defeat the disk limit.

A record larger than max_file_mb becomes an explicit log_record_omitted JSON record with its request ID, phase, byte count and SHA-256; the payload is omitted from the log without altering the actual request or response. Cleanup and I/O failures are reported on stderr and through last_error; traffic logging pauses on cleanup failure and retries, rather than growing past the budget or failing client requests. Deletion is permanent: archive any logs you need before first starting the upgraded relay or reducing a policy.

docs.title: Default Paths
docs.text:
• config: ~/.config/airelays/config.toml
  • data dir: ~/.airelays
  • logs dir: ~/.airelays/logs
  • OpenAI sign-ins: ~/.airelays/auth.json (first account) and ~/.airelays/accounts/<slug>/auth.json, owner-only files (see Security)
  • relay token file: ~/.airelays/relay-token
  • Claude account profiles: ~/.airelays/claude/accounts/<id>/ (metadata in account.json; the adjacent config/ is the profile's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR)
  • Claude setup token: ~/.airelays/claude-token, run from ~/.airelays/claude/token/config

Earlier singular AIRelay paths remain compatible for local upgrades.

docs.title: Sample Config
docs.text:
[server]
host = "127.0.0.1"
port = 8080

[paths]
data_dir = "~/.airelays"
logs_dir = "~/.airelays/logs"

[auth]
storage = "file"
browser_open = false
login_timeout_seconds = 900

[upstream]
base_url = "https://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex"
issuer_base_url = "https://auth.openai.com"
client_id = "app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann"
client_version = "auto"
request_timeout_seconds = 120.0

[security]
require_bearer_auth = true
bearer_token_file = "~/.airelays/relay-token"
auto_generate_bearer_token = false
rate_limit_per_minute = 120
rate_limit_burst = 40
concurrent_requests_per_ip = 8
failed_auth_window_seconds = 300
failed_auth_max_attempts = 8
failed_auth_block_seconds = 900
trust_x_forwarded_for = false

[uploads]
max_upload_bytes = 33554432
max_total_upload_bytes = 268435456

[logging]
# Opt-in: log every raw upstream SSE line. Hundreds of records per
# streamed response (~50x log growth under load); summary records
# (request, usage, response, errors) are always logged regardless.
stream_lines = false
retention_days = 7
max_total_mb = 1024
max_file_mb = 50

[providers.openai]
enabled = true
models_cache_ttl_seconds = 300.0
# Multi-account routing: "balanced" (default) routes to the account with
# the most remaining weekly quota so consumption equalizes as a
# percentage of each plan's capacity; "round_robin" sends equal request
# counts; "ordered" drains the first account first.
balance = "balanced"
# Extra model ids to advertise in /v1/models beyond the upstream catalog,
# for operator-confirmed models omitted from automatic discovery.
extra_models = []
# Fallback bench duration (seconds) when a limited account's reset time is
# unknown; upstream-reported reset times are used when available.
account_cooldown_seconds = 300
# Automatic retry for failed upstream LLM calls. Each retry re-runs the
# full account-pool failover pass, then waits the next backoff delay.
# 0 disables. A schedule shorter than the attempt count repeats its last
# delay. Retries only happen before any response byte reached the client
# (non-streaming requests, and the pre-header phase of streaming ones);
# retries that cannot succeed (a quota window that resets far beyond the
# backoff budget) are skipped so the honest 429 is not delayed.
retry_attempts = 3
retry_backoff_seconds = [5, 20, 60]
# Image generation (/v1/images/*): the per-image upstream timeout, and
# whether to read the image quota with a prompt-less probe (a free 400 that
# carries the quota headers) alongside each usage probe. Off, the image
# meter updates only when images are generated.
image_timeout_seconds = 300.0
image_usage_probe = true

[providers.claude]
enabled = false
bin = "claude"
command = []                          # full argv, wins over `bin` (see below)
timeout_seconds = 600.0
max_concurrent_requests = 2
balance = "balanced"                  # balanced, round_robin, or ordered
account_cooldown_seconds = 300         # retry delay when no reset time is reported
strip_api_key_env = true
models = ["claude:sonnet", "claude:opus", "claude:haiku", "claude:fable"]
oauth_token_file = "~/.airelays/claude-token"   # written by `airelays claude set-token`

docs.title: Provider Notes
docs.text:
[upstream] client_version = "auto" discovers the installed Codex CLI's version for model-catalog requests, with a tested minimum of 0.153.4 for standalone installations. The local version probe is bounded to three seconds and cached for five minutes. Updating Codex allows discovery to follow newer version-gated catalogs without adding model names to AIRelays. The former shipped value 0.124.0 is treated as auto, including existing desktop configuration files. Other explicit version pins are honored and can select an older catalog.

OpenAI runtime:

  • enabled by default
  • stores each sign-in as an owner-only file on every OS; storage only accepts file in practice (auto and keyring are read as file, and airelays doctor flags sign-ins an older version kept in the OS keyring)
  • airelays login manages its subscription session
  • caches successful upstream model-list responses for models_cache_ttl_seconds seconds by default
  • the model-list cache is process-local, in-memory, and disabled when models_cache_ttl_seconds = 0
  • cache state is visible under providers.openai.models_cache in GET /v1/relay/status
  • extra_models defaults to an empty list. Existing configured entries continue to extend a successful catalog and are deduplicated against it.

AIRELAYS_MODELS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS remains accepted as a shorter alias for AIRELAYS_OPENAI_MODELS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS.

Claude runtime:

  • discovers models and alias resolutions from the installed CLI, without generating text; its model catalog uses models_cache_ttl_seconds too
  • configured models extend discovery and remain available as fallback when CLI discovery is unavailable

  • use GET /v1/models?refresh=true or the desktop Models Refresh button to reload provider catalogs immediately

  • enabled by default; set [providers.claude].enabled = false or AIRELAYS_ENABLE_CLAUDE=false to opt out (requests still require the local claude CLI and at least one AIRelays Claude account)

  • uses the local claude CLI
  • airelays claude login adds an isolated account by running Claude Code's browser sign-in inside a new relay-owned profile; credentials remain CLI-owned
  • each account has its own CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, usage cache, model catalog, and max_concurrent_requests limit
  • balance defaults to balanced: available execution slots first, then lowest fresh weekly usage; round_robin rotates and ordered selects the first eligible profile in stable account-id order
  • AIRELAYS_CLAUDE_BALANCE and AIRELAYS_CLAUDE_ACCOUNT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS override the corresponding Claude configuration values
  • headless login: claude setup-token on a machine with a browser, then airelays claude set-token; the token is stored 0600 at oauth_token_file and runs as the inference-only account default in its own relay-owned configuration directory
  • only AIRelays-owned accounts are used: the personal Claude Code sign-in (~/.claude), an inherited CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN in the relay's environment are ignored
  • every claude process gets an explicit environment, its profile's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and a relay-owned working directory
  • finding claude: command (a full argv such as ["node", "/path/cli.js"]) wins; otherwise bin is looked up on PATH and in the usual install locations (~/.local/bin, ~/.claude/local, Homebrew, Volta, bun, nvm; on Windows %USERPROFILE%\.local\bin, Volta and WinGet). The path is used as found, so Claude Code's auto-updates keep working
  • Windows needs a real claude.exe; npm's claude.cmd shim is refused because cmd.exe would re-parse request text. Install Claude Code with its native installer, or set command to run node with the npm package's cli.js (desktop app: AIRELAYS_CLAUDE_COMMAND, since the app rewrites config.toml)
  • system prompts are passed through a private file when the CLI supports it; a request whose arguments still exceed the OS command-line limit gets 413 instead of a launch failure
  • usage comes from Claude Code's get_usage (verified with 2.1.292+); CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC in the relay's environment stops it and marks readings nonessential_traffic_disabled
  • follows the relay's protected or open local auth mode
  • served on the relay's listener (local or network); refused together with trust_x_forwarded_for
