docs.title: Does AIRelays use my OpenAI platform API key?
docs.text: No. The OpenAI runtime uses an AIRelays-owned ChatGPT subscription login.

docs.title: What token do I give my client?
docs.text: Use the AIRelays relay token from airelays init, airelays token show, or airelays token rotate.

docs.title: Where does AIRelays keep my sign-ins?
docs.text: In owner-only files in the data directory (~/.airelays by default), the same way on macOS, Linux and Windows. AIRelays does not use the OS keychain. See Credential Storage. If you used 0.16.0 or earlier, OpenAI accounts that version kept in the keychain need one new sign-in; airelays doctor lists them.

docs.title: Is AIRelays affiliated with any provider?
docs.text: No. AIRelays is an independent third-party project.

docs.title: How are requests spread across my OpenAI accounts?
docs.text: With more than one enrolled account, the relay routes each request to the account with the most remaining quota in its longest usage window — the weekly budget — among those that serve the requested model (the default, balance = "balanced"), so consumption equalizes as a percentage of each plan's own capacity — plans of very different sizes deplete proportionally. Which windows a plan reports is upstream policy (some plans report only a weekly window), so the relay ranks windows by duration rather than trusting their position in the payload. Usage is probed at launch and refreshed in the background; an account that reaches a limit on any window is benched until that window resets. Alternatives: balance = "round_robin" for strictly equal request counts, balance = "ordered" to drain the first account before the next. See Configuration.

docs.title: Can I disable relay auth?
docs.text:
Yes. Open local relay mode applies to all enabled providers, including the Claude runtime.

airelays init --no-auth
airelays serve --no-auth --port 8080

docs.title: Does AIRelays support Claude?
docs.text:
Yes, through the same OpenAI-compatible endpoint as GPT models.

  • discovered Claude aliases and concrete model ids, plus configured overrides
  • local claude CLI only
  • chat.completions, completions and responses
  • images, PDFs and text files as input; local files and conversations
  • function tool calls returned to your application, which runs them; AIRelays never runs a tool (see docs/api.md)
  • follows the relay's protected or open local authentication mode
  • served on the relay's listener, local or network
  • no image generation (GPT models only, see below)

docs.title: Can AIRelays generate images?
docs.text: Yes, on GPT models: POST /v1/images/generations and POST /v1/images/edits serve gpt-image-2 through the ChatGPT subscription with OpenAI's parameters (n, background, stream; size and quality are forwarded but the service picks its own and the relay discloses the difference). Images come back as PNG b64_json. The image quota is a separate 24-hour window, shown in the desktop and by airelays usage. Masks, audio and image variations are not available. See docs/capabilities.md.

docs.title: How do I log in to the Claude runtime?
docs.text:
Use the local Claude CLI through AIRelays:

  • browser login: airelays claude login; repeat to add another of your accounts
  • headless login: claude setup-token on a browser-equipped machine, then airelays claude set-token on the relay machine (stores the token in a 0600 file that survives service managers and reboots). It appears as the account default and is inference-only, without a usage bar

List accounts with airelays claude accounts, renew one with airelays claude login --replace ACCOUNT, and sign out one with airelays claude logout ACCOUNT. The desktop offers Sign in / Add account ("In a browser" or "With a token") and per-account sign-out. Each browser account is its own AIRelays-owned profile; signing out one leaves the others intact. airelays claude logout default only deletes the stored token.

docs.title: Does AIRelays use my Claude Code sign-in?
docs.text:
No. AIRelays never uses your personal Claude Code sign-in (~/.claude), an inherited CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, or an exported CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN, and it never signs Claude Code out. Switching or signing out Claude Code does not affect the relay. If you upgraded from 0.15.0 or earlier and Claude only worked through one of those, connect it once with airelays claude login or airelays claude set-token. AIRelays cannot copy the personal sign-in because Claude Code refresh tokens rotate. Profiles already enrolled keep working.

Claude requests balance across eligible accounts with capacity. The relay uses fresh weekly usage when available, rotates when usage is unknown, and can fail over before response bytes reach the client. Subscription tokens remain subscription tokens; adding accounts does not enable API-key auth.

docs.title: Can I see my Claude subscription usage?
docs.text: Yes: GET /v1/subscription/status?provider=claude returns the 5-hour and weekly windows in the same normalized shape as OpenAI usage. The desktop app shows per-account usage in the OpenAI and Anthropic cards. Use ? beside an account name for details. Readings come from each profile's Claude Code (get_usage, verified with 2.1.292+) every five minutes and are marked stale with a reason when Claude returns no live data. Setup-token accounts report no usage. See Subscription Status.

docs.title: Is using my subscription through AIRelays allowed by the providers?
docs.text: AIRelays does not certify that your use is permitted. Personal, local, or noncommercial use and a successful login do not by themselves establish authorization. Your provider's terms govern access methods, automation, credential handling, and workloads; permission for its own CLI or SDK does not necessarily cover every part of AIRelays. Unauthorized use may lead to account suspension or termination, and compatibility may change without notice. See the disclaimer for the access mechanisms used by each runtime and official terms to review.

docs.title: How do I control reasoning depth?
docs.text: Set reasoning_effort in your request to one of the model's supported modes. Every model's modes and default are published in /v1/models under airelays.reasoning, shown in the desktop Models tab, and listed by airelays models. Supported modes vary by model and are read from provider catalogs when available, including max and ultra where reported. Omitted effort uses the provider's default; Claude can use an adaptive default. See API notes for details.

docs.title: Which model is behind a Claude alias?
docs.text: The Models tab and airelays models show the concrete model reported by the installed Claude CLI. For example, a CLI can resolve claude:fable to claude-fable-5-1. The alias follows CLI updates and account settings; the discovered concrete id pins that version. Use Refresh to query the CLI again. A configured label means the catalog did not confirm that selector, so AIRelays does not claim a concrete resolution for it.

docs.title: Does AIRelays support Gemini?
docs.text: No.

docs.title: Why does the dashboard disappear when I click another window?
docs.text: The dashboard hides when it loses focus; the relay keeps running and unsaved edits remain in the window. On macOS and Windows, left-click the tray icon to reopen it, or right-click for the menu. Open Dashboard is available in the tray menu on all platforms. In Overview, Connect Your App contains both connection details and the authentication/network access controls.

docs.title: Are output-token limits enforced?
docs.text: Yes, on both account types. max_completion_tokens, max_tokens (chat and completions) and max_output_tokens (/v1/responses) are enforced by the providers themselves: GPT models apply the limit upstream (the minimum is 16), and on Claude models the run stops when the model reaches the limit. An answer cut by the limit reports finish_reason: "length" (status: "incomplete" on /v1/responses), as on OpenAI. See Capabilities.

docs.title: Why did I get 401 and then 429?
docs.text: The relay token was missing or wrong, and repeated bad attempts triggered the temporary IP block.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: This guide covers the CLI/server install. If you prefer a GUI, the desktop app (macOS, Windows, Linux) wraps the same relay with a system tray, dashboard, and one-click sign-in — see the README's install section for its one-line installers and desktop/README.md.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
One line on macOS or Linux, without sudo:

curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lpalbou/AIRelays/main/scripts/install-headless.sh | bash

The script installs the newest PyPI release into an isolated environment (uv tool or a Python 3.11+ virtualenv) and links ~/.local/bin/airelays. Set AIRELAYS_VERSION=X.Y.Z to pin a release; run it again to upgrade.

From PyPI directly:

python -m pip install airelays

From a source checkout:

python -m pip install .

docs.title: Initialize AIRelays
docs.text:
airelays init

This prepares:

  • config: ~/.config/airelays/config.toml
  • data dir: ~/.airelays
  • logs dir: ~/.airelays/logs
  • relay token: ~/.airelays/relay-token

Show the current relay token at any time:

airelays token show

docs.title: Custom Configuration
docs.text:
The CLI and desktop use the same saved accounts and relay configuration by default. To use another configuration, pass --config consistently when signing in, inspecting accounts, and starting the relay:

airelays --config ./relay.toml init
airelays --config ./relay.toml claude login
airelays --config ./relay.toml claude accounts --json
airelays --config ./relay.toml serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080

Shared options such as --config and --data-dir work before or after subcommands. A later explicit value takes precedence. See Configuration for paths and environment overrides.

docs.title: OpenAI Runtime
docs.text:
Log in:

airelays login

On a server or over SSH (no local browser), use device-code login — you approve the sign-in from a browser on any other device:

airelays login --device

airelays login selects the device flow automatically on SSH sessions and displayless Linux. The browser flow's URL only works in a browser on the same machine as the relay (its redirect targets localhost:1455 there).

You can enroll several of your own OpenAI accounts: running airelays login again with a different account adds it alongside the first, and the relay balances across them (see the README's "Multiple OpenAI Accounts" section). Sign an account out with airelays logout <email>; manage order and capacity holds with airelays accounts.

Start the server:

airelays doctor
airelays serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080

Verify:

curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/models \
  -H 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_AIRELAYS_TOKEN'

curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_AIRELAYS_TOKEN' \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "gpt-5.5",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly: OPENAI AIRelays OK"}]
  }'

docs.title: OpenAI Open Local Relay Mode
docs.text:
airelays init --no-auth
airelays login
airelays serve --no-auth --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080

In this mode AIRelays does not require Authorization on /v1/*. Open local relay mode applies to all enabled providers, including the Claude runtime.

docs.title: Claude Runtime
docs.text:
AIRelays uses only Claude accounts it owns. Add one with a browser sign-in:

airelays claude login
airelays claude login       # optional: add another of your own accounts
airelays claude accounts

Each sign-in creates a separate Claude Code profile under ~/.airelays/claude/accounts/<id>/. Claude Code owns its credentials and refreshes them. The desktop offers Sign in / Add account → "In a browser" in the Anthropic card. Usage bars need a Claude Code version that supports get_usage (verified with 2.1.292+); requests work without it.

Headless Claude login — claude setup-token needs a browser, so run it on any machine that has one, then carry the token to the server:

# on a machine with a browser:
claude setup-token

# on the server:
airelays init
airelays claude set-token   # paste the token; stored 0600, survives restarts

The token is stored in ~/.airelays/claude-token and appears as the account default (desktop: "With a token"). It is inference-only: Claude reports no usage or email for setup tokens, so it has no usage bar and cannot be deduplicated against browser accounts.

Your personal Claude Code sign-in (~/.claude), an inherited CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and an exported CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN are never used; airelays doctor reports an ignored CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. Until an account is connected, claude:* requests return 503 provider_auth_error.

Manage one account using its email or id from airelays claude accounts:

airelays claude login --replace ACCOUNT
airelays claude logout ACCOUNT

Renewal requires the same account and pauses that profile until sign-in succeeds. To renew the setup token, run airelays claude set-token again. Duplicate browser subscriptions receive only one share of traffic.

Signing out runs claude auth logout inside that AIRelays profile only; airelays claude logout default only deletes the stored setup token. Neither touches your personal Claude Code sign-in. Use --all only to sign out all AIRelays accounts. The running relay discovers account changes automatically and balances requests across eligible accounts with capacity.

Start AIRelays with the Claude runtime enabled:

airelays serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080

Verify:

curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_AIRELAYS_TOKEN' \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "model": "claude:sonnet",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Reply with exactly: CLAUDE AIRelays OK"}]
  }'

Current Claude limits:

  • runs through the claude CLI on the relay's machine
  • served on the relay's listener, local or network
  • follows the relay's protected or open local authentication mode
  • no audio, no image generation (GPT models only), no server-side tools (web search), no forced tool calls

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
Inspect relay and provider readiness:

airelays status

Usage windows of the running relay, including the image-generation quota:

airelays usage

docs.title: Image Generation
docs.text:
GPT models also generate and edit images through OpenAI's Images routes:

curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/images/generations \
  -H 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_AIRELAYS_TOKEN' \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt": "a watercolor fox", "quality": "low"}'

The image comes back as PNG b64_json; /v1/images/edits takes the image to change as a multipart file. See API Notes.

Run local setup checks plus live upstream probes:

airelays doctor

airelays doctor checks config, relay-token state, OpenAI login readiness, upstream /models, a tiny /responses smoke request, and Claude readiness when the Claude runtime is enabled. Use airelays doctor --skip-response to skip the response smoke request.

List every model id the running relay accepts, grouped by provider:

airelays models

Machine-readable output:

airelays status --json
airelays doctor --json
airelays models --json

airelays status shows:

  • relay config and token state
  • OpenAI runtime readiness
  • Claude runtime readiness when enabled
  • next recommended commands

docs.title: Provider Routing
docs.text:
• models starting with claude: use the Claude runtime when it is enabled
  • other model ids use the OpenAI runtime when it is enabled
  • AIRelays rejects requests when the selected runtime is disabled or the route is outside that runtime's published subset

docs.title: Client Configuration
docs.text:
Base URL:

http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1

Standard OpenAI SDKs can use the AIRelays relay token through their normal api_key field when the base_url points at AIRelays.

Example shell setup:

export OPENAI_BASE_URL='http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1'
export AIRELAYS_TOKEN="$(tr -d '\n' < ~/.airelays/relay-token)"

docs.title: Subscription Status
docs.text:
OpenAI subscription usage:

curl http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/subscription/status \
  -H 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_AIRELAYS_TOKEN'

Claude subscription usage (same normalized shape):

curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/subscription/status?provider=claude' \
  -H 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_AIRELAYS_TOKEN'

See Subscription Status for multi-account parameters and the payload shape.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
AIRelays separates two authority domains:

  • upstream provider auth
  • local client access to AIRelays itself

The upstream subscription login is not the relay access credential.

docs.title: Protected Routes
docs.text:
Protected by default:

  • /v1/*
  • /no-tools/v1/*

Public:

  • /
  • GET /healthz

Detailed diagnostics live behind GET /v1/relay/status unless you intentionally launch an open local relay.

docs.title: Relay Token
docs.text:
The normal path is:

airelays init

Show the current token:

airelays token show

Rotate it:

airelays token rotate

docs.title: Credential Storage
docs.text:
AIRelays stores its secrets the same way on macOS, Linux and Windows (ADR 0008):

  • OpenAI sign-ins, the relay token and the Claude setup token are files in the data directory. On macOS and Linux the directories AIRelays creates are owner-only (0700) and the files are created owner-only (0600); on Windows they inherit the user profile's permissions, so keep the data directory inside your profile.
  • Files are replaced atomically, and a lock file next to each sign-in keeps two AIRelays processes (for example the tray relay and a CLI command) from refreshing the same rotating token at once.
  • AIRelays does not use the OS keychain, Credential Manager, or Secret Service. Protection at rest comes from file permissions and disk encryption; enable FileVault, BitLocker, or LUKS if the machine may be lost.
  • Claude browser sign-ins stay with Claude Code, which keeps them in the macOS keychain or in each profile's folder on Linux and Windows (see Claude Guardrails).

docs.title: Open Local Relay Mode
docs.text:
Open local relay mode applies to all enabled providers, including the Claude runtime.

airelays init --no-auth
airelays serve --no-auth --port 8080

Equivalent environment override:

AIRELAYS_REQUIRE_BEARER_AUTH=false airelays serve --port 8080

docs.title: Claude Guardrails
docs.text:
When the Claude runtime is enabled:

  • the relay's protected or open local auth mode applies
  • trust_x_forwarded_for is rejected
  • each request is a fresh CLI run with session persistence and built-in tools off; client tool calls are returned, never run (see docs/api.md)
  • the runtime runs the claude CLI on the relay's machine and is served on the relay's listener; in network mode, devices on your network can use your Claude accounts, so keep the API key required there

AIRelays uses only Claude accounts it owns: profiles added through airelays claude login, each with its own CLI-owned credential store, and an optional setup token stored 0600 by airelays claude set-token. The personal Claude Code sign-in, an inherited CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and an inherited CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN are never used. AIRelays stores identity metadata and usage state beside each profile. It never reads Claude credentials (no keychain or credential-file reads) and does not implement OAuth login or refresh; usage comes from Claude Code's get_usage request inside each profile. Signing out runs claude auth logout only inside that relay-owned profile, or deletes the stored setup token; it never signs out the personal Claude Code or other accounts.

Every Claude Code process runs with an explicit environment, its profile's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and a relay-owned working directory. Processes are ended gracefully (stdin closed or SIGTERM before SIGKILL) so a token refresh in progress can finish. Claude Code still derives a few files from the home directory (for example device keys) regardless of CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. On macOS, run the relay in your login session, not over SSH or as a LaunchDaemon, so Claude Code can use the keychain.

docs.title: Desktop Updates
docs.text: The desktop app's update check reads the public GitHub Releases list for lpalbou/AIRelays; it sends no account, token, or usage data. An in-place update installs only the release that check offered, and the installer refuses a download whose SHA-256 differs from the digest GitHub publishes for that release asset. Downloads are trusted through HTTPS to GitHub; the installers are not code-signed. See desktop/README.md.

docs.title: Rate Limits
docs.text:
Default single-process protections:

  • 120 requests/minute per IP
  • burst 40
  • 8 concurrent requests per IP
  • temporary IP block after repeated bad tokens

docs.title: Upload Ceilings
docs.text:
• 32 MiB per file
  • 256 MiB total stored file bytes

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
AIRelays logs:

  • inbound requests
  • provider resolution
  • endpoint rejects
  • provider and upstream requests
  • provider and upstream responses
  • provider stream lines
  • usage summaries

Request and response contents, including prompts and model outputs, can be written to the local AIRelays log files. Raw bearer tokens are redacted. The logs directory is owner-only, like the rest of the data directory.

Traffic logs default to a 7-day age limit and 1 GiB disk budget, with hourly/ 50 MiB rotation. The oldest whole files are permanently deleted, including eligible logs already present when upgrading. Use the tray's retention controls, airelays logs, or the authenticated /v1/relay/logging API to change the policy. This is log retention only; stored uploads and conversations are separate. See configuration for details.

docs.title: Subscription Status
docs.text:
AIRelays exposes:

  • GET /v1/subscription/status
  • GET /v1/account/rate_limits (alias)

Both providers report usage in one normalized shape, so a client can render OpenAI and Claude quota with the same code: per-window used_percent, window_label ("5h", "weekly", derived from each window's duration), and reset times (reset_after_seconds, reset_at_iso).

docs.title: OpenAI
docs.text:
Reads the OpenAI subscription usage surface at chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage.

Which windows appear is plan-dependent upstream policy: some plans report a 5h window plus a weekly window, others only a weekly window. AIRelays passes through exactly the windows the upstream reports — nothing is synthesized — and identifies each by its duration, not its position in the payload. Multi-account balancing and the desktop's per-account token breakdown both key on the longest reported window (the weekly budget).

credits, spend_control, rate_limit_reset_credits, and model_usage preserve the upstream's credit and model-availability facts. Available limit-reset credits and credits applicable right now are distinct counts. Quota percentages are not token counts or monetary balances. The desktop's token breakdown counts only responses observed through this relay in the account's reported window, not activity in other apps or before recording.

docs.title: Usage resets
docs.text:
OpenAI sometimes grants Codex users a usage reset (shown as "Redeem reset" in Codex): a credit that restarts the account's usage windows. AIRelays reads these from the same subscription and lets you redeem one without opening an OpenAI app:

  • GET /v1/relay/accounts/resets lists each account's credits with their title, who granted them, grant and expiry times, and whether the upstream would apply one right now (redeemable_now); see API
  • POST /v1/relay/accounts/resets/redeem spends one; the upstream's answer (reset, nothing_to_reset, no_credit, already_redeemed) is reported verbatim and the account's usage is re-read at once
  • CLI: airelays accounts resets and airelays accounts redeem <email>
  • Desktop: an account holding a reset shows N usage reset available under its bars with what it is and when it expires, and a Redeem now button that asks for confirmation. The ? panel keeps the counts.

A credit held while usage is below its limit is available but not applicable: redeeming it answers nothing_to_reset and keeps the credit. The relay never redeems on its own.

curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/subscription/status' \
  -H 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_AIRELAYS_TOKEN'

With multiple enrolled accounts:

  • ?account=<email-or-prefix> selects one account
  • ?all_accounts=true returns the list shape with one entry per account, regardless of how many are enrolled; an account whose usage probe fails carries an error string instead of a status, so one broken sign-in never hides the others (releases before 0.12.5 folded a lone account to the bare single-account shape)
  • ?raw=true includes the raw upstream payload

docs.title: Image generation quota
docs.text:
Image generation on the ChatGPT subscription is metered in its own upstream bucket (imagegen_premium, a 24-hour window observed live), not in the text windows above, and the usage endpoint does not report it. The image routes do, in every response's headers, so AIRelays reads the quota there and reports it as rate_limits.image_generation in the same window shape, with:

  • source: image_response when the reading came with an image, probe when it came from the relay's quota probe
  • observed_at: when that reading was taken
  • relay: the images this relay produced on the account in the last window (images, requests, image_tokens), from its own records

The probe is a prompt-less image request the upstream refuses with 400 without spending quota; the refusal carries the quota headers. It runs with each usage probe (cached for a minute; every five minutes in the background with several accounts) so the meter stays current between image requests. Set [providers.openai] image_usage_probe = false to turn it off; the meter then updates only when images are generated. Readings survive restarts (~/.airelays/openai-image-usage.json).

The desktop shows the quota as an Images · 24h window bar under each OpenAI account, with the relay's image count and the reading's source in the ? details; airelays usage prints the same windows in the terminal. An exhausted image bucket benches the account for images only; text requests keep flowing, and the other way round.

docs.title: Claude
docs.text:
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/subscription/status?provider=claude' \
  -H 'authorization: Bearer YOUR_AIRELAYS_TOKEN'

Returns the 5-hour and weekly windows, plus named scoped caps such as Fable, Sonnet, or Opus when the subscription reports them. The modern limits array supplies explicit scope names and percentages; legacy buckets remain supported. A Fable cap at 100% does not mean the whole Claude allowance is exhausted. The desktop names the exhausted scope instead of presenting all Claude models as unavailable.

Add &all_accounts=true for a per-account list ({"object": "subscription_status_list", "provider": "claude", "accounts": [...]}), or &account=<email-or-id> for one account. Each list entry contains slug, email, and one of status, error, or usage_unsupported. The setup-token account (default) always carries usage_unsupported: Claude reports no usage or email for setup tokens, so &account=default returns 422 unsupported_for_provider and the desktop explains this instead of showing bars. Each browser-enrolled account has its own set of bars.

spend and extra_usage preserve usage-credit status, disabled reasons, and reported amounts. Hover over or activate ? beside an account name in the OpenAI or Anthropic section to open details; press Escape to close. These details format money only with its declared currency and decimal scale (amount_minor / exponent in spend, or decimal_places in extra_usage). A missing balance or limit is not inferred from zero spend. Notes:

  • requires the Claude runtime to be enabled and an AIRelays-owned account; the personal Claude Code sign-in is never read or reported
  • usage comes from Claude Code itself: the relay sends each profile's CLI the Claude Code SDK get_usage control request — no prompt, no inference, no quota. AIRelays never reads Claude credentials (no keychain or credential-file reads) and never calls the usage endpoint directly
  • readings refresh at startup and every five minutes. Claude Code renews a profile's OAuth token while answering, so this also keeps idle accounts signed in
  • requires a Claude Code version that supports get_usage (verified with 2.1.292+); Claude Code marks it experimental. Older versions report the meter as unsupported without affecting requests
  • failed refreshes back off exponentially (5, 10, 20, 40, then 60 minutes), persisted across restarts; refreshing the desktop does not bypass this
  • usage state and backoff are separate for each profile; an unavailable usage meter does not imply unavailable inference

docs.title: Freshness
docs.text:
captured_at records the successful fetch time, not each cache read. The Overview refreshes usage every five minutes while open; its reset countdowns use absolute reset timestamps. Missing percentages, or windows whose reset has passed without fresh evidence, display awaiting fresh data, not zero usage. Neither catalog membership nor a quota snapshot guarantees the next request will succeed.

A Claude reading is fresh only when Claude Code returns live data. Otherwise the dashboard and API show the last good reading, including its scoped caps, marked stale with its age and a stale_reason:

  • usage_unavailable: Claude did not return live data, for example because the upstream rate-limited its usage endpoint
  • nonessential_traffic_disabled: CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC is set in the relay's environment, which stops Claude Code fetching usage
  • cli_unsupported: the installed Claude Code lacks get_usage; update Claude Code (requests are unaffected)
  • cli_failed: the CLI is missing, timed out, or failed

Without any good reading yet, the API returns an error message instead of numbers. Stale readings never unblock or rank an account, and capacity observations older than fifteen minutes do not rank accounts; a known exhausted window still blocks routing until its reset or a newer fresh reading shows capacity.

docs.title: Auth
docs.text: Default protected mode requires the relay bearer token, as shown above. Open local relay mode (--no-auth) accepts the same requests without the Authorization header.

docs.title: Desktop app install
docs.text:
The desktop builds are not notarized (macOS) or code-signed (Windows), so the operating system may warn when you install them by hand. The one-line installers in the README avoid these prompts on macOS and Linux.

  • macOS says "AIRelays is damaged" or "cannot be verified" after you downloaded the DMG in a browser: clear the quarantine flag, then open the app again.
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/AIRelays.app

Alternatively, open System Settings → Privacy & Security and choose Open Anyway for AIRelays. - The installer reports that no desktop installer exists for your system: desktop builds cover Apple Silicon Macs, x86_64 Linux, and x64 Windows. On other machines, including Intel Macs, use the headless installer (scripts/install-headless.sh); it runs the same relay without the tray. - Windows SmartScreen blocks the setup .exe: choose More info → Run anyway, or use the PowerShell installer. - Windows, AIRelays 0.18.0 and earlier: the relay shows Failed and the Console tab (or an OpenAI sign-in) reports ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'threading'. Those Windows builds shipped an incomplete embedded Python. Install 0.19.0 or later by running the PowerShell installer again; your accounts and settings are kept. - Linux: the AppImage does not start from a terminal with a FUSE error: install libfuse2 (libfuse2t64 on Ubuntu 24.04), or run it with APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1. The menu entry created by the installer already does this when FUSE 2 is missing. GNOME needs the AppIndicator extension to show the tray icon. - The headless installer warns that ~/.local/bin is not on your PATH: add export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" to your shell profile and open a new terminal.

docs.title: A desktop update did not install
docs.text:
AIRelays reopens on the version you had and shows why the update failed. The full log is ~/.airelays/update/update.log.

  • "Checksum mismatch": the download did not match the digest GitHub publishes. Nothing was installed. Retry later from About.
  • "Check for updates again before installing": the dashboard was open across a new release; choose Check for updates, then update.
  • The updater does not start (for example where policy blocks PowerShell scripts): run the one-line installer from the README, or download the installer from the release page.

docs.title: Traffic logs report a cleanup error
docs.text:
The tray Settings page or GET /v1/relay/logging can report last_error, or airelays logs can print a cleanup error. AIRelays pauses traffic-log writes until it can enforce the configured limit; relay requests continue normally.

Check that the configured log directory is writable and has space available:

airelays logs
airelays status --json

If the limit is smaller than the history you need, archive the relevant log files first, then raise the total limit or shorten retention:

airelays logs --retention-days 30 --max-total-mb 2048 --max-file-mb 50

Use the same --config, --data-dir, or --logs-dir arguments as the running relay. Apply the policy again, then confirm that last_error is empty and over_budget is false. See traffic-log retention for the policy, ownership boundaries, and permanent-deletion behavior.

docs.title: A model is missing or a Claude alias is unclear
docs.text:
Use the Models tab's Refresh button or GET /v1/models?refresh=true to reload both provider catalogs. OpenAI discovery uses client_version = "auto" by default; an explicit older version pin can select an older catalog. Update the installed Codex CLI to follow newer catalogs.

For Claude, update the configured claude CLI and inspect the alias's airelays.resolved_model in /v1/models. Concrete ids are also listed. If discovery fails, inspect providers.claude.models_discovery_error in GET /v1/relay/status; configured ids and the last successful catalog remain available. See model discovery and configuration.

docs.title: "Another AIRelays relay is already running with the data directory …"
docs.text:
Only one relay can use a data directory at a time, so accounts, uploads, conversations and logs are never shared between two relays. The message gives the running relay's process id, and the command exits with status 75. The desktop app reports this case with a notification and does not retry.

  • if the desktop app is running, it already runs the relay: use that one, or quit the app first (tray menu → Quit AIRelays)
  • if a terminal session runs airelays serve, stop it first
  • to run two relays on purpose, give each its own --data-dir

docs.title: 401 Missing or invalid AIRelays bearer token
docs.text:
• run airelays status
  • run airelays doctor --skip-response
  • confirm the relay token is present
  • confirm the client is calling http://HOST:PORT/v1/...
  • use airelays token show if needed

docs.title: 503 No ChatGPT login found
docs.text:
• run airelays status
  • run airelays doctor --skip-response
  • if the OpenAI runtime is enabled, run airelays login
  • on a server or over SSH, run airelays login --device
  • if the browser flow cannot bind localhost:1455, use airelays login --device

docs.title: An OpenAI account is missing after upgrading to 0.16.1
docs.text:
AIRelays 0.16.1 and later store OpenAI sign-ins only as owner-only files (ADR 0008). Sign-ins that 0.16.0 or earlier kept in the OS keychain, Credential Manager, or Secret Service are no longer read.

  • run airelays doctor --skip-response; it lists those accounts under openai_keyring_sign_ins
  • sign in again with airelays login (or Sign in in the desktop app), once per account
  • you can remove the old AIRelays Auth entries from your OS keychain afterwards

docs.title: I opened the login URL on my laptop and got a connection error at localhost:1455
docs.text:
The browser flow's sign-in redirect goes to localhost:1455 on the machine running the browser — pasting the URL into a browser on another computer sends the redirect to the wrong machine, so the login on the server never completes and eventually times out.

Two fixes:

  • Device-code login (recommended): airelays login --device prints a short code you approve from a browser on any device. This is the default on SSH sessions and displayless Linux.
  • SSH tunnel (if you specifically need the full browser flow, e.g. for a browser-profile picker): run ssh -L 1455:localhost:1455 user@server first, then open the printed URL in your local browser. The tunnel can be opened even after airelays login has started waiting.

docs.title: Claude CLI not found, or a .cmd shim is refused (Windows)
docs.text:
• run airelays doctor --skip-response; the Claude check shows which claude the relay found
  • AIRelays looks for claude on PATH and in the usual install locations; a claude installed after the tray started is found after a relay restart
  • on Windows, install Claude Code with its native installer (claude.exe). npm's claude.cmd shim is refused because cmd.exe would re-parse request text; to use an npm install, set [providers.claude].command to ["node", "<path to the package's cli.js>"]; with the desktop app, set the AIRELAYS_CLAUDE_COMMAND environment variable to the same JSON array instead, because the app rewrites config.toml
  • a 413 on a Claude request means its system prompt or JSON schema exceeds the OS command-line limit; shorten it

docs.title: 503 No Claude account is connected to AIRelays
docs.text:
AIRelays uses only Claude accounts it owns. Your personal Claude Code sign-in (claude auth login or /login), an inherited CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and an exported CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN are ignored, so signing in to Claude Code does not connect the relay. Until an account is connected, claude:* requests return 503 provider_auth_error and /v1/models lists no Claude models.

  • run airelays claude login (desktop: Sign in → "In a browser") once per subscription
  • on a headless host or under systemd/docker, run claude setup-token on any machine with a browser, then airelays claude set-token (desktop: "With a token"); the token is stored 0600 in ~/.airelays/claude-token
  • airelays doctor reports a CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN set in the relay's environment; AIRelays ignores it

After upgrading from 0.15.0 or earlier, installs that relied on the personal sign-in or an exported token need this once. Claude Code refresh tokens rotate, so AIRelays cannot copy the personal sign-in. Profiles already enrolled keep working, and switching or signing out Claude Code does not affect the relay.

docs.title: A Claude request fails: which account or model is affected
docs.text:
AIRelays decides what a Claude CLI failure affects before taking any account out of rotation, and the error message says which case applies:

  • Your request (a bad image, an unreachable URL, a prompt that is too long): 422 or 413 explaining what to change. No account is paused.
  • One model on one account: the API does not serve that model to the account (a "not found" or permission refusal while a live usage check shows the account's sign-in works). Only that model is paused on that account (unavailable_models in /v1/relay/status); other models keep working, and another account is tried. If none can serve it, you get 404 model_unavailable; use another model from /v1/models.
  • A passing sign-in refusal: the CLI reported a sign-in error, but the live usage check shows the sign-in works (for example a token that was just renewed). Nothing is paused; another account is tried, and retrying usually works.
  • An account's usage limit or a temporary failure: the account pauses until its reset time (or account_cooldown_seconds when the reset is unknown), or about 30 seconds after a temporary failure, and another account is tried. The message lists each account's state, with Retry-After; a wait over a minute also carries x-should-retry: false. When the check cannot tell whether the sign-in works, the account pauses the same way.
  • An account's sign-in: the usage check confirms the sign-in was rejected (an explicit authentication error, such as a revoked token). The account is marked as needing a new sign-in, leaves rotation until you sign in again, and the message names the command to run (see below).

docs.title: 502 invalid_json_output on a Claude model
docs.text: You asked for response_format: {"type": "json_object"} and the model's answer was not a single JSON object. AIRelays checks JSON-mode answers before returning them, so you never receive broken JSON with a success status. Retry the request, or send json_schema with a schema: the Claude CLI enforces named schemas natively.

docs.title: A Claude request with tools fails with 502 cli_tools_unavailable
docs.text:
The Claude CLI could not load the request's tools, so AIRelays stopped the request instead of answering without them.

  • check each tool's parameters: it must be a JSON Schema of type object (other shapes are refused with 422)
  • the tool helper is a small file inside the installed AIRelays package, started with the relay's own Python: if the installation was moved or partly removed, reinstall AIRelays (or the desktop app)
  • retry the request; the error names the tools that were missing

502 cli_unexpected_tools means the CLI reported or attempted a tool that AIRelays did not define. The request was stopped before anything ran; update AIRelays and the Claude CLI, then retry. Neither error pauses an account.

docs.title: 422 for an image or document
docs.text:
Both runtimes check images and documents before any upstream call.

  • images must be PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, as a base64 data: URL, an http(s) URL, or a file_id from POST /v1/files; a wrong declared type is corrected automatically
  • documents (file parts) must be PDFs or UTF-8 text files
  • on Claude models, "Claude could not read N of the M images or documents" means the CLI could not process a file (for example a CMYK JPEG or an animated image): convert it to a standard PNG, JPEG or PDF and retry

docs.title: An answer stops early with finish_reason: "length"
docs.text:
The request set an output-token limit (max_completion_tokens, max_tokens, or max_output_tokens on /v1/responses), and the model reached it. Both account types enforce the limit, as OpenAI does.

  • raise the limit, or remove it to let the model finish
  • on GPT models the minimum is 16; lower values return the upstream's 400
  • check your client's defaults: some SDK helpers set a small max_tokens

docs.title: A Claude account needs to sign in again
docs.text:
Use airelays claude accounts to find the account id, then airelays claude login --replace ACCOUNT. Choose the same account in the browser. A different identity is not eligible for requests through the enrolled profile. To add another subscription, use airelays claude login without --replace. The desktop offers Sign in again on unavailable profile rows. For the setup-token account (default), run claude setup-token and airelays claude set-token again.

Do not move or rename a profile's config/ directory: the path identifies its macOS Keychain entry. After a machine migration, sign in again on the new host. On macOS, run the relay in your login session (the desktop app does), not over SSH or as a LaunchDaemon, so Claude Code can use the keychain. An unavailable usage meter alone does not require signing out.

docs.title: A Claude usage bar is stale or missing
docs.text:
Usage comes from each profile's Claude Code (get_usage). A stale bar shows the last good reading with its age; the reason is stale_reason in GET /v1/subscription/status?provider=claude&all_accounts=true:

  • usage_unavailable: Claude returned no live data (for example, the upstream rate-limited its usage endpoint). Retries back off from 5 to 60 minutes; requests are unaffected
  • nonessential_traffic_disabled: remove CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_NONESSENTIAL_TRAFFIC from the relay's environment
  • cli_unsupported: update Claude Code (verified with 2.1.292+)
  • cli_failed: check that the configured claude binary runs; see airelays doctor

The setup-token account never has a bar (Claude reports no usage for setup tokens); add a browser profile with airelays claude login for a meter. Stale readings never unblock or rank an account.

docs.title: Desktop app shows "Sign-in expired" on an OpenAI account
docs.text:
OpenAI ended that account's stored session (for example after signing in to Codex elsewhere), so the relay can no longer refresh its token. The account is out of rotation until you sign in again.

  • click Sign in again next to the badge and pick the same account in the browser — the stored sign-in is replaced in place, no sign-out needed
  • the usage bars return within a few seconds of a successful sign-in
  • the raw upstream error is available on hover over the note under the row
  • from the CLI, airelays login does the same repair: signing in with an already-enrolled account refreshes that account's stored credentials

docs.title: Desktop app shows "Running — not responding"
docs.text:
The relay process is alive but did not answer the app's health probe — usually heavy system load or a long request burst.

  • it recovers on its own once the relay answers again; the label flips back to "Running"
  • if it persists, open the Console tab for relay output, or use Restart
  • Stop/Restart keep working: the app still manages the process

docs.title: 404 model_not_found or 422 on chat and completions
docs.text:
A 404 with code model_not_found means the model id is not available: confirm it appears in /v1/models (a discovered alias, concrete claude-* id, configured override, or an OpenAI model your account's catalog lists).

A 422 names what the relay cannot honor. Checks:

  • on Claude models: remove audio, a forced tool call (tool_choice required or a named tool), parallel_tool_calls: false, strict: true tools, non-function tools, and previous_response_id (use conversation); an image Claude cannot read (corrupt, CMYK, animated) must be converted to a standard PNG, JPEG or PDF
  • remove stop, logprobs, top_logprobs, logit_bias, web_search_options and moderation: neither upstream can honor them, so AIRelays rejects them rather than returning output that ignores them
  • remove other unsupported generation controls

If a request succeeds but behaves as if a parameter were missing, check the x-airelays-ignored-parameters response header: it lists every parameter AIRelays dropped, including ones it does not recognize.

docs.title: Cursor custom OpenAI endpoint errors
docs.text:
If Cursor is configured to call AIRelays as a custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint and Agent/Edit flows fail, first identify which malformed request family you are seeing.

AIRelays 0.12.2 and later accepts the two Cursor request shapes reported publicly by Cursor users and staff on February 26, 2026 and July 9, 2026:

  • full Responses-style bodies sent to /v1/chat/completions
  • flat Responses-style custom tools / tool choices / tool calls on the chat route (for example ApplyPatch)

AIRelays 0.12.3 and later also strips unsupported top-level caller identity fields (user, safety_identifier) before the upstream request and rejects OpenAI model ids that are absent from a working live /v1/models catalog, instead of letting those failures happen upstream.

Checks:

  • if you see Only function tools are currently supported on chat routes., upgrade AIRelays
  • if you see Unsupported parameter: user, upgrade AIRelays; current versions strip user (and safety_identifier) locally because the ChatGPT/Codex backend does not accept caller-supplied end-user ids
  • if you see The '...model...' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account., compare the chosen model against GET /v1/models; with a working upstream catalog AIRelays now rejects unsupported OpenAI ids locally and only [providers.openai].extra_models should bypass that check. On multi-account relays, if you just added or removed an account, current versions refresh that admission cache automatically before deciding
  • inspect the traffic log under ~/.airelays/logs/... for a compatibility_adaptation record showing the chat route accepted a Responses-shaped body
  • if the request mixes both messages and input, AIRelays rejects it loudly; that payload is ambiguous and must be fixed at the client
  • if a role:"tool" message does not reference a preceding assistant tool call in the same request, AIRelays rejects it as malformed instead of guessing the wrong tool type
  • if Cursor still fails after the normalization above, capture the inbound request body from the traffic log and compare it with the documented supported shapes in docs/api.md

docs.title: Claude startup refusal
docs.text:
When the Claude runtime is enabled:

  • keep the listener on 127.0.0.1, localhost, or ::1
  • keep relay bearer auth enabled
  • keep trust_x_forwarded_for=false

docs.title: 429 Too many invalid authentication attempts from this IP
docs.text:
• wait for the Retry-After window
  • update the client to the correct relay token
  • rotate the token if needed

docs.title: 413 on uploads or requests with files
docs.text:
• confirm the file is below the per-file upload ceiling
  • confirm the relay has not reached the total stored-upload quota
  • 413 request_too_large on a Claude request: the images and documents in one request (inline or by file_id) are limited to 32 MiB in total, the Claude API's request limit; split the files across requests

docs.title: 502 / 429 with server_is_overloaded or usage_limit_reached, or slow answers while the upstream is degraded
docs.text:
• the upstream itself is failing or out of quota; the error body carries the upstream's own code and message
  • before surfacing the error, the relay retried automatically (default 3 retries waiting 5s/20s/60s, each re-running account failover), which is why a failing request can take a minute or more before answering — check the traffic log for retry_backoff / retry_skipped / upstream_stream_error records to see what happened
  • tune or disable with retry_attempts / retry_backoff_seconds ([providers.openai], or desktop Settings → Providers)
  • a 429 that names a reset far in the future is not retried (waiting a minute cannot help a window that resets in hours); with several accounts enrolled, the message reports the earliest account recovery
  • a 400 invalid_request_error (for example an input that exceeds the model's context window) is answered immediately with the upstream's own error: it is deterministic, so it is never retried, never rotated to another account, and never benches an account — fix the request instead
  • "All N OpenAI accounts are at their limits" is only claimed when every account is benched by real limit evidence (a quota rejection or the usage report); rounds of transient upstream failures answer "All N OpenAI accounts failed for this request" instead

docs.title: Live upstream verification
docs.text:
Use airelays doctor when local state looks correct but client requests still fail. It checks local setup, then verifies the OpenAI upstream /models route and runs a tiny /responses smoke request when the OpenAI runtime is enabled and logged in.

airelays doctor

Use airelays doctor --skip-response when you want setup and model-list checks without sending a generation request.

docs.title: ADRs
docs.text:
• 0001: No Silent Degradation, Truncation, Or Budget Invention

docs.title: 0001: No Silent Degradation, Truncation, Or Budget Invention
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-06-12

docs.title: Context
docs.text: This project sits between OpenAI-compatible clients and a different upstream surface with real behavioral differences. A compatibility layer can easily become misleading if it silently drops parameters, truncates user content, invents token budgets, or fakes support for unsupported endpoints.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The server must not silently:

  • truncate file content
  • invent token budgets or usage numbers
  • coerce unsupported binary/audio payloads into text
  • treat unsupported routes as successful no-ops
  • hide upstream constraints that materially affect semantics

When a behavior cannot be reproduced honestly, the server must:

  • reject the request with an explicit error, or
  • document the exact adaptation being performed when the adaptation is minimal and required for basic interoperability

docs.title: Required Consequences
docs.text:
• text-like uploaded files larger than 1 MB are rejected instead of truncated
  • unsupported endpoints return explicit 501 unsupported_error
  • unverified modalities return 422 or 501, not silent best-effort guessing
  • usage is logged only when the upstream provides it
  • upstream store=true is rejected because the verified subscription backend requires store=false
  • the minimal placeholder instructions value "." may be injected only when the caller omitted instructions entirely and only because the verified upstream rejects an empty instructions field

docs.title: Rationale
docs.text: The project is more useful when it is slightly narrower but trustworthy than when it appears broader while silently changing behavior.

docs.title: 0002: ChatGPT Subscription Backend Compatibility Boundary
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-06-12

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The user requirement is an OpenAI-compatible server that relies on a ChatGPT subscription login, not on a user-supplied OpenAI platform API key. The actual verified backend available through the reused login protocol is the ChatGPT Codex backend, not the general OpenAI platform API.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The project will:

  • use the ChatGPT Codex backend as the primary upstream
  • reuse the upstream login and token refresh protocol without sharing Codex-owned local storage
  • expose only the OpenAI-compatible routes that were verified against that upstream
  • reconstruct non-stream responses locally because the verified upstream requires streaming
  • provide explicit unsupported responses for unverified routes

The project will not:

  • claim full parity with every OpenAI platform endpoint
  • pretend that platform API scopes are available when they are not
  • silently reroute unsupported calls into different semantics

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• /v1/models, /v1/responses, and /v1/chat/completions are first-class compatibility targets
  • local files and local conversations are part of the compatibility layer because the upstream surface does not provide full OpenAI file/session parity
  • some OpenAI endpoints remain intentionally unsupported until they are verified against the subscription backend

docs.title: 0003: Local Config And Default-Deny Relay Security
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
AIRelays is a local OpenAI-compatible relay backed by a reused ChatGPT subscription login. That upstream login is necessary for provider access, but it is not a safe or coherent credential for client-to-relay access.

The project also needed a cleaner end-user setup story than raw environment variables alone.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
AIRelays adopts these rules:

  1. Relay-client authorization is separate from upstream provider authorization.
  2. Protected API routes default to bearer-token enforcement.
  3. The relay bearer token is local state owned by AIRelays, not by the upstream provider auth store.
  4. AIRelays exposes a small local control plane through:
  5. ~/.config/airelays/config.toml
  6. CLI overrides
  7. AIRELAYS_* environment variables
  8. AIRelays applies single-process in-memory abuse controls at the edge:
  9. per-IP request rate limits
  10. per-IP concurrent-request caps
  11. temporary IP blocks after repeated bad tokens
  12. Listener default remains loopback-only.

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• End users get a repeatable first-run setup with airelays init.
  • Relay access can be rotated independently from upstream login state.
  • Abuse controls apply before request bodies are parsed or upstream calls are made.
  • Future provider adapters can remain behind one stable client-facing relay boundary.

docs.title: Negative
docs.text:
• AIRelays now owns a small amount of local secret state.
  • Rate limiting is single-process and not distributed across multiple instances.
  • Setup and docs must explain two credential layers clearly.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Multi-tenant access control
  • Distributed rate limiting
  • Shared remote operations control plane

docs.title: 0004: Provider Runtime Boundary And Experimental Local Adapters
Status
docs.text:
Accepted

Amended 2026-07-10: the Claude adapter graduated out of the "experimental" label when it merged to mainline (user-facing labels, the experimental wire fields, and the env-var name changed; AIRELAYS_ENABLE_CLAUDE_EXPERIMENTAL remains honored as a legacy alias). The rules below still bind the Claude adapter unchanged — explicit model-driven routing, visible capability boundaries, local-only/loopback-only operation, stateless default, and explicit rejection of unsupported combinations. Only the labeling and the "reject open-relay mode" clause (superseded by the relay-wide auth-mode behavior documented in README and docs/security.md) have evolved.

Amended 2026-10-18 (0.19.0): the "loopback-only" clause is withdrawn. The user's choice of listener applies to every provider: a relay bound to the network serves Claude models to the network too, under the same relay auth mode. The relay still runs the local claude CLI on its own machine, and the Claude runtime is still refused together with trust_x_forwarded_for. The desktop app no longer pauses Claude in network mode.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
AIRelays now exposes more than one upstream runtime behind one OpenAI-compatible local edge. The OpenAI runtime remains the primary subscription-backed path, while Claude support is introduced as a smaller local adapter with a materially different auth surface and capability boundary.

Without an explicit rule, future provider work would drift into ambiguous model routing, overstated parity claims, or provider-specific behavior leaking into shared routes without a clear contract.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
AIRelays adopts these rules for multi-provider expansion:

  1. Provider selection is explicit and model-driven.
  2. claude:* model ids select the Claude experimental runtime when it is enabled.
  3. Other model ids select the OpenAI runtime when it is enabled.
  4. Provider capability boundaries must be visible in /v1/models and /v1/relay/status.
  5. Unsupported provider, route, state, or parameter combinations must fail locally and explicitly.
  6. Experimental local adapters must be:
  7. opt-in
  8. local-only
  9. loopback-only
  10. bearer-auth-required
  11. stateless by default
  12. AIRelays must not claim blanket parity across providers.
  13. AIRelays may use provider-owned local login state or provider-approved local tokens, but must not silently store or invent a separate provider session model unless a later ADR allows it.

docs.title: Positive
docs.text:
• AIRelays can serve more than one subscription-backed runtime from one local server.
  • Users can discover provider ownership and route limits from the model catalog itself.
  • Experimental adapters can ship with narrow, explicit limits without weakening the richer OpenAI path.

docs.title: Negative
docs.text:
• The shared northbound API is no longer universal across all enabled providers.
  • Docs, CLI output, and runtime diagnostics must stay explicit about provider-specific setup and route support.
  • Adding future providers will require deliberate routing, capability, and security decisions instead of silent fallback.

docs.title: Enforcement
docs.text:
• /v1/models must include provider identity and route capability metadata.
  • /v1/relay/status must expose provider-scoped readiness.
  • Provider-specific route handlers must reject unsupported combinations explicitly.
  • User-facing docs must state the current provider-routing rule and the experimental/local-only status of narrow adapters.
  • Experimental local adapters must reject open-relay mode.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• Tests for provider routing and provider-specific route rejection
  • Tests for provider readiness reporting
  • Tests for Claude experimental guardrails
  • Live smoke checks for one OpenAI request and one Claude request through the same AIRelays process

docs.title: Context
docs.text: AIRelays writes redacted traffic records as JSONL files. Files rotate hourly, but a busy relay can create substantial disk usage unless logs also have a retention policy. The relay can run from the CLI or through the desktop tray, and the tray regenerates its relay configuration before launch.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The relay owns traffic-log retention. The CLI, authenticated relay API, and desktop Settings page use the same saved policy in the log directory.

The policy has three limits:

  • retention_days limits file age;
  • max_total_mb limits total managed traffic-log contents;
  • max_file_mb rotates an active log file before it exceeds the configured size.

The defaults are 7 days, 1024 MiB total, and 50 MiB per file. Both age and size limits apply, and the oldest managed files are deleted first. Cleanup runs at startup, periodically while the relay is running, when a file rotates, and when the policy changes.

Policy updates are atomically saved as <logs_dir>/.retention.json. That policy overrides the corresponding TOML defaults so tray configuration generation cannot replace a live API or CLI update. A process lock coordinates policy updates, rotation, writes, and cleanup among relay processes that share the log directory.

Cleanup manages only AIRelays traffic files in the documented date-based layout. It does not follow symlinks or manage hard links, console output, uploads, conversations, or unrelated files. A record too large for one log file is represented by an explicit omission record containing its request ID, phase, original size, and digest. If cleanup cannot enforce the policy, traffic logging pauses and reports the error; serving requests continues.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
The same bounded behavior applies to standalone and tray-managed relays without requiring a platform-specific log-rotation service. Existing eligible traffic logs are evaluated on the first upgraded start, so users should archive any history they need before enabling or tightening retention.

Retention removes complete files permanently. It provides an upper bound on traffic-log contents rather than a guaranteed number of days of history: a busy relay can reach the size limit before the age limit. All writers sharing a log directory must use a retention-aware AIRelays version; external writers and older relay versions are outside this policy.

See Configuration for operation and API Notes for the HTTP contract.

docs.title: Status
docs.text:
Accepted, 2026-09-26. Extends ADR 0004.

Amended 2026-10-10 by ADR 0007: the ambient Claude Code sign-in is no longer an account, the default slug now names only the stored setup token, and usage comes from Claude Code itself.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: One user may have several Claude subscriptions. Claude Code supports isolated configuration directories, including directory-scoped macOS Keychain entries. AIRelays needs to select accounts without sharing credentials across requests or taking ownership of Anthropic's OAuth flow.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• airelays claude login delegates to the unmodified CLI's subscription login with a unique, stable CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR.
  • Enrollment metadata lives at data_dir/claude/accounts/<id>/account.json. It contains identity and a revision, never OAuth tokens. The adjacent config/ directory and its credential store remain owned by Claude Code.
  • The existing CLI/token setup is the implicit default account. Global token overrides apply only to it. No existing credential is moved.
  • Reauthentication suspends a managed profile until its original identity is verified. Renewing default creates an isolated profile without changing the default CLI sign-in or headless token.
  • One Claude account pool selects account-specific CLI runtimes. Model catalogs, usage caches, persisted usage backoff, and concurrency limits are isolated per profile. A duplicate subscription is counted once.
  • Selection honors model eligibility and fresh usage, with rotation when quota is unknown. Request failures can fail over only before output reaches the client; invalid request shapes do not trigger account rotation. Known exhausted windows stay blocked until reset even when the meter ages.
  • Logout targets one profile through the CLI and removes enrollment only after successful logout. Multiple-account logout needs a target or --all. Profile directories are retained because they may contain CLI-owned state.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text:
A generic pool shared with OpenAI would require changing its HTTP/SSE backend contract and auth storage model. Separate provider pools keep those boundaries explicit while reusing the existing Claude request adapter.

One relay process per account would isolate credentials but require another routing service and duplicate ports, supervisors, and usage reporting.

Direct subscription-token inference would remove subprocess overhead but depends on an unsupported inference/authentication integration. It is outside this decision. Account isolation does not establish provider permission for every relay workload; the existing intended-use boundary still applies.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Existing single-account configuration remains usable. Adding profiles is reversible through targeted logout, without moving the default CLI credentials. Credential-store behavior and usage reporting remain dependent on the installed Claude Code version; failed usage probes cannot be treated as zero consumption. Claude remains local, stateless, subscription-backed, and without API-key auth.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted, 2026-10-10. Amends ADR 0006.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
ADR 0006 kept the user's own Claude Code sign-in as an implicit default account. That made the relay depend on a personal tool it does not own:

  • Switching the personal Claude Code login to another subscription silently changed which subscription the relay served and reported. When it switched to an account already enrolled as a profile, the relay deduplicated default away, and a subscription reachable only through it disappeared.
  • Signing out default from AIRelays signed out the personal Claude Code.
  • Usage meters read OAuth access tokens directly from Claude Code's credential stores and never refreshed them. A profile that served no requests showed its last numbers indefinitely after its access token expired; only default stayed fresh, because the personal session kept rotating its token.

Claude Code refresh tokens rotate, so one credential cannot be shared or copied between the personal sign-in and a relay profile.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• AIRelays routes only through accounts it owns: profiles enrolled with airelays claude login (each with its own CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR under data_dir/claude/accounts/<id>/) and, optionally, one setup token stored with airelays claude set-token. The ambient Claude Code sign-in, an inherited CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and an inherited CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN are never used. Existing installs that relied on them must add an account.
  • The setup-token account keeps the default slug for API compatibility. It runs in its own relay-owned configuration directory (data_dir/claude/token/config). It is inference-only: Claude reports no usage and no identity for setup tokens, so it has no meter and cannot be deduplicated. Signing it out only deletes the stored token.
  • AIRelays never runs claude auth logout outside a relay-owned profile.
  • AIRelays never reads Claude credentials. Usage comes from the Claude Code SDK control request get_usage (skip_behaviors), run inside each profile. The CLI refreshes the profile's OAuth token as needed, without an inference request. The background usage refresh therefore also keeps idle profiles signed in.
  • get_usage is experimental in Claude Code. A reading counts as fresh only when it carries the limits list or a breakdown as_of under two minutes old; anything else (a snapshot the CLI seeded after an upstream failure, a null meter, an unsupported CLI) keeps the last good reading, marked stale with its age and reason. Stale data never unblocks or ranks an account. Failures back off exponentially, persisted across restarts. There is no fallback to reading tokens or calling the usage endpoint directly.
  • Every Claude Code process runs with an explicit environment and a relay-owned working directory. Processes are ended gracefully (stdin closed or SIGTERM) before any SIGKILL, so the CLI can finish persisting a rotated token.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Copying the personal sign-in into a profile would split one rotating refresh token between two owners; the first refresh breaks the other. Refreshing tokens in AIRelays would take ownership of Claude Code's OAuth flow and its credential stores. A periodic inference request would keep tokens alive but open usage windows and spend quota.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: The personal Claude Code sign-in and AIRelays are independent in both directions. Adding the first account requires one browser sign-in per subscription (or a setup token). Usage reporting depends on Claude Code supporting get_usage; older versions report the meter as unsupported without affecting requests. Claude Code still derives a few files from the home directory (for example device keys) regardless of CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. On macOS the relay must run in the user's login session so Claude Code can use the keychain.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted, 2026-10-11. Complements ADR 0003 and ADR 0007.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
AIRelays runs on macOS, Linux and Windows, as a headless CLI relay and as a tray app that supervises the same relay. Several mechanisms behaved differently per OS in ways users could not see:

  • OpenAI sign-ins were stored in the OS keyring first and a file second. Windows Credential Manager cannot hold an OpenAI token set (its blob limit is smaller than the record), macOS ties each keychain item to the interpreter that last wrote it and prompts any other one, and a locked Linux keyring can block the relay. Two stores also let a rotated refresh token diverge.
  • claude child processes were started with a POSIX-shaped environment and argv, which breaks name resolution and launches on Windows, puts system prompts in the process list, and fails on argument-size limits.
  • Data directories were created with default permissions.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• One mechanism per concern, on every OS. Per-OS behavior is expressed as data (path lists, environment names, process flags) behind one abstraction, and is the same in CLI and tray modes.
  • Credentials are private files. OpenAI sign-ins are stored only as files under the data directory: directories AIRelays creates are owner-only (0700), files are created owner-only (0600) and replaced atomically, and a separate lock file serializes refresh-then-save across processes. On Windows protection comes from the user profile's ACL. There is no keyring storage mode and no fallback between stores. AIRelays does not read the OS keyring; sign-ins an older version stored there are reported as needing a new sign-in. Claude credentials stay owned by Claude Code (ADR 0007).
  • One launcher for claude. An explicit claude_command wins; otherwise the executable is resolved at relay start (and again after a failed launch) from the inherited PATH and known install locations, never pinned to a versioned path. Windows uses a real executable and refuses .cmd/.bat shims. The child PATH starts with the directory where claude was found. The child environment comes from one allowlist with per-OS additions, matched case-insensitively only on Windows. Large or sensitive inputs leave the command line where the CLI supports it; requests that still exceed the OS argument limit are rejected with 413. Windows children start without a console window.
  • The bundled interpreter is isolated (-I -B -u -X utf8) whenever the tray starts the relay or a CLI command.
  • Packaging is valid by default. The macOS bundle carries a valid ad-hoc signature checked in CI until it is Developer ID signed and notarized; Windows installers remain unsigned until code signing is added.
  • Tests run on all three OSes in CI.
  • Next, in this order: an opt-in stdin lifeline for graceful relay shutdown and orphan prevention, one relay per data directory, a single-instance tray, and per-user service installation for headless use.

docs.title: Alternatives
docs.text: Keeping the keyring as an opt-in store would preserve encryption at rest on macOS and some Linux desktops, but keeps per-OS failure modes, prompts and hangs that a relay cannot recover from on its own. An automatic keyring import would still need to read the keyring, which can prompt or block; a new sign-in is simpler and explicit.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text: Sign-ins behave the same on every OS and in every mode, and no keyring prompt or lock can stall the relay. Tokens are protected by file permissions and disk encryption rather than the OS keyring. OpenAI accounts that an older version stored in the keyring must sign in again once.

The provider-runtime expansion is complete and released: the ChatGPT subscription path is the primary runtime (with balanced multi-account routing) and the Claude runtime is a first-class local adapter as of 0.4.0. Open work is the cross-platform runtime track (ADR 0008) plus proposed hardening follow-ups.

Metadata
docs.text:
• Created: 2026-07-11
  • Status: Completed

  • Version: unreleased at completion (targeting the next minor release)

docs.title: ADR status
docs.text:
• Governing ADRs: 0001 (no silent degradation), 0003 (local security defaults)
  • ADR impact: none required — routing strategy is configuration, not durable policy

docs.title: Context
docs.text: With two enrolled OpenAI accounts, production traffic logs showed whole hours in which one account received every request while the other idled, and a saturated account receiving live traffic again right after the desktop Refresh action. An adversarial three-track investigation of the code and the JSONL traffic logs established two root causes: the ordered default strategy (which the desktop-rendered config could not override — it never wrote a balance key), and the refresh path clearing every usage-limit bench before re-probing, opening a window in which the ordered picker routed to the known-exhausted account (observed twice, each earning an extra 429).

docs.title: What we did
docs.text:
• Default balance = "round_robin", implemented as least-recently-selected (fair under membership churn, unlike a shared modulo counter over a changing list). "ordered" remains opt-in. Values are normalized and validated at startup.
  • The desktop app writes the balance key into the rendered config, exposes it in Settings, and its Accounts card caption/badges reflect the actual mode.
  • Evidence-gated bench lifecycle: the refresh action re-probes first and releases only accounts whose fresh usage shows capacity; a stale snapshot cannot erase a newer bench; benching reads every reached-limit signal in the payload and waits for the longest exhausted window.
  • Failover classification covers account-scoped failures beyond HTTP errors: transport failures become structured 502s, dead credentials (AuthenticationError, persistent 401) bench and fail over, the last attempt is benched too, fallbacks try healthy accounts first, and usage-limit markers are only trusted structured or on a real 429.
  • Robustness: benches survive pool reloads, retired HTTP clients are closed, sticky-map eviction replaces the all-at-once wipe, transient cooldowns cannot truncate longer benches, account_selected records carry an attempt index, and the refresh action writes an accounts_refresh record.
  • Launch-time warm-up: a multi-account pool probes each account's usage and model catalog in the background at startup (account_pool_warmed record), so balancing and model-aware routing are correct from the first request.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• pytest -q — 165 passed (19 new pool/config tests covering balancing fairness, evidence-gated releases, failover classes, marker scoping, warm-up)
  • Live verification on a spare port against real accounts: balanced selection across both accounts, transparent failover on a real 429, evidence-gated refresh keeping the exhausted account benched, and a fresh process benching the at-limit account at launch with zero upstream errors

docs.title: Residual risks / follow-ups
docs.text:
• OpenAI usage probes have no cache/single-flight; see proposed item 0013.
  • Benches use the monotonic clock and freeze across system sleep; see proposed item 0014.
  • ~~An in-stream upstream failure event (HTTP 200 + response.failed) does not trigger failover; latent, never observed in logs.~~ Observed live 2026-08-01 (server_is_overloaded window on gpt-5.6-sol): non-streaming lanes returned the failed response as an empty HTTP 200. Fixed in two steps: collect_response now raises a structured BackendError (429 for usage-limit codes, else 502), which the pool classifies for failover/benching like any upstream HTTP error, and failure events are logged as upstream_stream_error traffic records. The pool's streaming generator now buffers pre-content events (response.created, response.in_progress) and converts a failure event or silent death before the first content event into the same raised error — benching and failing over exactly like the non-streaming path — so failover honesty is keyed on client-visible bytes, not on the first upstream event. Failures after content started remain in-band (failover would be dishonest); automatic retry (retry_attempts) re-runs the whole pool pass in the pre-header phase.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Add a short per-account TTL cache and single-flight to the OpenAI subscription-usage path, mirroring the guardrails the Claude usage path already has (cache, fetch lock, attempt spacing, retry-after handling).

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: /v1/subscription/status is public relay API and each call hits the upstream usage endpoint once per account with no protection. Current desktop cadence is trivial (fetches on mount/refresh only), but any client scripting the route at a poll cadence would generate thousands of upstream hits per hour per account, plausibly triggering upstream throttling on a personal account. Cheap probes would also make proactive benching affordable at higher frequency.

docs.text: ChatGptCodexBackend.get_subscription_status (src/airelay/backend.py) fetches unconditionally; OpenAiAccountPool.subscription_statuses (src/airelay/accounts.py) loops accounts per call. Compare ClaudeCliRuntime usage guardrails in src/airelay/providers.py.
