• 15–30s per-account TTL cache with single-flight in the pool

  • keep _bench_from_usage semantics unchanged (probe-start gating already in place)

Every probe also feeds _bench_from_usage, so proactive limit-benching now happens continuously instead of only on manual status loads. docs.title: Context
docs.text: After the round-robin default shipped, live usage showed the intended limit: request counts were exactly equal (verified in traffic logs: 199/199 completed requests, ~1.0M tokens each side over two hours), yet the Plus account's 5h window climbed to 25% while the Enterprise account sat at 1% — equal request counts drain a small plan many times faster than a large one.   • round_robin (strictly equal counts) and ordered (spillover) remain as explicit opt-ins; config validation, desktop settings select, Accounts-card captions, and CLI summaries describe all three.

• Created: 2026-07-28

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
The upstream usage payload became plan-dependent (observed live 2026-07-28 in traffic logs): a Plus account reports its weekly window alone in rate_limit.primary_window (the plan has no 5h window anymore), while an Enterprise account keeps the classic 5h primary plus a weekly secondary. Item 0016's balanced strategy read the capacity signal from the primary slot, which now mixed a weekly percentage against a 5h percentage — incomparable quantities that, early in a fresh week, would route sustained traffic into the small plan's scarce weekly budget. The per-account token tally was anchored to the primary window's reset_at; for accounts still reporting a 5h primary, that wiped the breakdown every bucket roll, leaving the desktop's "more" panel permanently empty (confirmed: openai-window-tokens.json held "models": {} for both accounts despite 754 completed requests / 8.2M tokens served that day). The desktop also synthesized an idle "5h window" row whenever only long windows were present — a fabrication for plans that no longer have a 5h window.

Owner-reported symptom for the record: the Plus weekly bar at 91% with the Enterprise at 4%. Traffic-log analysis showed the relay itself routed 97% of that day's requests to the Enterprise account (23 vs 754), so the burn was mostly external to the relay — but the signal mixing, the wiped tally, and the fabricated idle row were all real defects.

docs.title: What we did
docs.text:
• New airelay/usage_windows.py: typed parsing of rate_limit windows (UsageWindow, parse_rate_limit_windows, longest_window) plus the shared window_label. Windows are identified by limit_window_seconds, never by slot position.
  • Balanced routing signal = used_percent of each account's longest-horizon window (the weekly budget every current plan shape shares). Short-window exhaustion stays covered by proactive benching (any window >= 100% still benches until the longest exhausted window resets) and reactive 429 failover. Integer bucketing, least-recently-selected ties, 15-minute signal max-age, sticky conversation affinity all unchanged. A payload without windows updates nothing (signal ages out; tally keeps its window).
  • Token tally anchored to the longest window's reset_at, with window_seconds/window_label persisted and exposed on the window_tokens snapshot (scope is now current_usage_window_via_this_relay). STATE_VERSION stayed 1: the schema change is additive and old 5h-anchored entries self-correct on the first probe.
  • Desktop: only reported windows render (idle-row synthesis removed); the "more" panel title names the tally window (e.g. "This weekly window, via this relay"); mock mode carries the two real plan shapes plus an exhausted at-limit account.
  • pytest testpaths hygiene so a bare run no longer crawls into gitignored desktop runtime bundles.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• Two-agent adversarial pass (implementer + independent adversarial reviewer): reviewer approved with no blocking/major findings after driving _bench_from_usage, the tally, and the parser with both live payload shapes and adversarial ones (missing durations, bool/string percents, equal durations, windowless payloads, upgrade paths).
  • pytest -q — 208 passed (15 new tests: real-shape signal extraction, mixed-pool routing, rotation fallback, tally anchor semantics across 5h rolls and weekly rolls, snapshot label, parser unit tests, pre-upgrade state-file compatibility).
  • Playwright render of mock mode: Plus card shows exactly one Weekly bar, Enterprise shows 5h + Weekly, at-limit badge renders, "more" panel populated under the weekly title, no horizontal overflow.
  • Live verification after install on the production relay (real accounts).

docs.title: Residual risks / follow-ups
docs.text:
• A transient payload that drops the weekly window while keeping a 5h one would re-anchor the tally destructively (clear on the way out and back). No such shape observed live; hardening would require anchor changes from a shorter window to persist across two consecutive probes.
  • Balancing compares weekly percentages across plans whose absolute weekly quotas differ; that is the intended definition of balanced charge (percentage of each plan's own capacity), not a defect.
  • Item 0014 (wall-clock bench expiry across system sleep) remains proposed and now also affects multi-day weekly benches.

Metadata

• Created: 2026-10-10
  • Status: Completed

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
ADR 0006 kept the personal Claude Code sign-in as an implicit default account beside the browser-enrolled profiles. An owner with two Claude subscriptions had one of them reachable only through that personal sign-in. When the personal Claude Code login switched to the other subscription, which was already enrolled as a profile, the relay deduplicated default away and the first subscription disappeared from routing and from the dashboard.

At the same time, the enrolled profile's usage meter had been frozen for more than three days: it still showed 19% weekly usage when the real value was 62%, and a per-model weekly cap at 16% when it was really exhausted (100%). The relay read OAuth access tokens directly from Claude Code's credential stores and never refreshed them; a profile that served no requests kept its last numbers after its access token expired. Only default stayed fresh, because the personal session kept rotating its token. Signing out default from AIRelays also signed out the personal Claude Code.

Refresh tokens rotate, so the personal sign-in cannot be shared with or copied into a relay profile. The decision is recorded in ADR 0007.

docs.title: What we did
docs.text:
• Accounts are only those AIRelays owns: browser-enrolled profiles under data_dir/claude/accounts/<id>/ and an optional setup token stored with airelays claude set-token. The personal Claude Code sign-in, an inherited CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and an inherited CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN are never used; airelays doctor reports an ignored CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.
  • The setup token keeps the default slug for API compatibility, runs in its own relay-owned data_dir/claude/token/config, and is inference-only: no meter (usage_unsupported, 422 unsupported_for_provider for account=default) and no deduplication.
  • Sign-out runs claude auth logout only inside a relay-owned profile; logout default only deletes the stored token. With no account connected, claude:* requests return 503 provider_auth_error and /v1/models lists no Claude models.
  • Usage comes from the Claude Code SDK get_usage control request inside each profile, at startup and every five minutes. AIRelays no longer reads Claude credentials or calls the usage endpoint. The CLI renews the profile's token while answering, so the refresh also keeps idle profiles signed in.
  • A reading is fresh only with live data; otherwise the last good reading is served stale with its age and stale_reason (usage_unavailable, nonessential_traffic_disabled, cli_unsupported, cli_failed). Failures back off 5 → 10 → 20 → 40 → 60 minutes, persisted across restarts. Stale readings, including scoped caps, never unblock or rank an account.
  • Relay status: oauth_token_source is profile or file, managed_profile is false for the setup-token account, served_by is removed, and duplicate_of remains.
  • Every Claude Code process runs with an explicit environment, its profile's CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR, and a relay-owned working directory, and is ended gracefully (stdin closed or SIGTERM before SIGKILL).
  • User-facing docs, llms.txt, llms-full.txt, and the changelog describe the account boundary, the usage source and stale reasons, and the one-time migration for installs that relied on the personal sign-in.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• ADR 0007 accepted; ADR 0006 marked as amended.
  • pytest: 417 passed. New coverage: ambient sign-in, config dir and env token never become accounts; zero accounts answer claude:* with 503; live vs. seeded get_usage readings; exponential backoff persisted across restarts; unsupported CLI and disabled nonessential traffic; usage refresh surviving caller cancellation; a real child process answering a control request and exiting cleanly on stdin close (no kill); setup-token sign-out deleting only the token file without running any CLI command.
  • Desktop: 14 browser tests (setup-token row and sign-out copy, signed-out profile renewal), 3 node usage tests, cargo check.
  • Live check against Claude Code 2.1.296 with a real enrolled profile: only the browser profile is discovered (the personal sign-in is ignored), every process uses the profile's config dir, and get_usage returns a live reading in under two seconds without inference, including a per-model cap at 100% that the frozen meter had shown at 16%.
  • Documentation checked for real identifiers before publication (public repository).

docs.title: Residual risks / follow-ups
docs.text:
• Verify on a profile idle for more than eight hours that get_usage renews its token: the profile's keychain item modification time changes, and an inference request succeeds afterwards.
  • Consider folding the 30-second --version and auth status probes into one CLI session to reduce process launches (backlog only).
  • get_usage is experimental in Claude Code; a removal or shape change would turn every meter stale (cli_unsupported) without affecting requests.
  • Claude Code still derives a few files from the home directory (for example device keys) regardless of CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. On macOS the relay must run in the user's login session to use the keychain.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Three adversarial reviews (one per OS) of AIRelays in CLI and tray modes found that several mechanisms only worked on some platforms: OpenAI sign-ins kept in the OS keyring could not be saved on Windows (Credential Manager's size limit), prompted on macOS for every other interpreter, and could block the relay on a locked Linux keyring; claude children received a POSIX-shaped environment that breaks on Windows, put system prompts in the process list, and failed on argument limits; airelays init wrote unparsable TOML with Windows paths; data directories were readable by other local users; the macOS app's signature was invalid; tests ran on Linux only.

docs.title: What we did

docs.title: Context
docs.text: A client reading OpenAI's standard usage names recorded every OpenAI-runtime call through AIRelays as 0 prompt / 0 completion tokens. The chat and completions routes translated the Responses API output but passed its usage through verbatim (input_tokens, output_tokens, a nested attribution block). The Claude runtime used the standard names but counted only the uncached prompt tokens the Claude CLI reports, missing cache reads and writes (2 reported for a 3,542-token prompt), and invented zeros when usage was missing. Streamed usage chunks kept a non-empty choices list, and /v1/completions streams ignored include_usage.

docs.title: What we did
docs.text:
• One CompletionUsage section in airelay.transforms: ints-only counts, two explicit source adapters (Responses usage, whose input_tokens already include cached tokens; Anthropic usage, whose input_tokens exclude cache reads and writes), details only when reported, usage omitted when unreadable, unknown upstream keys dropped (kept in traffic logs).
  • Streaming follows stream_options.include_usage: usage: null on every chunk, one final choices: [] chunk after the finish_reason chunk and before [DONE], on chat and completions for both runtimes.
  • Claude usage comes only from the CLI's result event; streamed Claude requests now log outbound_usage.

  • stream_options without streaming is dropped and disclosed in x-airelays-ignored-parameters; truncated non-streaming responses report finish_reason: "length". /v1/responses is unchanged.

  • Conformance pass beyond usage (schema validation against openai-openapi plus an adversarial audit): OpenAI error objects everywhere (with a detail copy), 404 model_not_found, Retry-After, Claude sign-in failures as non-retryable 503, Claude streams primed before the 200, content_filter and refusals mapped, required logprobs/refusal fields, integer created, and stop/logprobs/top_logprobs/ logit_bias rejected instead of silently ignored (seed disclosed). Unsupported features keep 422 per ADR 0001 (the spec defines no error status codes).

  • Third conformance round (adversarial audit with the openai-python SDK): conversations keep their whole history (ConversationTurn in airelay.conversations), assistant content: null with tool calls, files.list pagination and form-field purpose, GET /v1/models/{model}, file content parts, allowed_tools, verbosity/prompt_cache_key, the deprecated functions round trip, unknown parameters disclosed through per-route parameter sets (both runtimes), strict-only schema normalization, Retry-After from upstream resets_in_seconds, non-retryable 501s, and x-request-id.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: OpenAI-compatible clients send image_url content parts and tools to any model. GPT models accept both. Claude models reject both with 422 because the Claude runtime pipes a plain-text transcript into claude -p. The goal is to behave like an OpenAI endpoint as far as the Claude CLI genuinely allows.

docs.title: Evidence (live probes, CLI 2.1.299)
docs.text:
• --input-format stream-json (requires --output-format stream-json) accepts image blocks: PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP, several images in order, an image in an earlier transcript turn, and {"type": "url"} sources. Plain text gives the same result, usage and stop reason as -p text input; --system-prompt, --effort and --json-schema still work, and partial messages still stream.
  • The CLI silently replaces images it cannot process (corrupt data, CMYK JPEG, animated WebP) with a text notice and reports success. --replay-user-messages shows what it actually sent.
  • Each stream-json user line is a separate, separately billed model call.
  • Tools: a stub MCP server (--mcp-config, built-in tools off with --tools "", --permission-prompts none) makes the client's tools visible; the model emits native tool_use blocks, including parallel calls, before any execution. Stopping the CLI at message_delta with stop_reason: "tool_use" captured every call with zero executions. Prior calls and results rendered as transcript text lead to a correct final answer and to new native calls on later turns.

docs.title: Plan
docs.text:
1. One Claude runner: stream-json in and out for every request, one stdin line (the transcript as content blocks), stdout read with a large line limit and stopped at the first result event; the separate JSON runner is removed. The request is prepared once per request, not per account.
  2. One shared image module for both runtimes: data URL, local file_id, https URL or the string shorthand, validated (strict base64, magic-byte format sniffing to PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP, configurable size and count caps), then written as Responses input_image or a Claude image block. Invalid images get 422 on both runtimes, as on OpenAI. On Claude, --replay-user-messages turns any image the CLI dropped into a 422. detail is ignored on Claude and listed in x-airelays-ignored-parameters.
  3. Tools on Claude: the stub MCP server ships in the package and runs with the relay's own interpreter; the relay aborts if the CLI's init event lists any tool other than the stubs, strips the mcp__relay__ prefix, returns OpenAI tool_calls with finish_reason: "tool_calls", and takes usage from the streamed message events. Prior calls and results are rendered into the transcript. Rejected with 422: tool_choice required or named, parallel_tool_calls: false, strict: true, custom tools. The run ends with the stream-json interrupt control request at stop_reason: "tool_use", then stdin closes (a SIGKILL leaves the CLI's session record behind until a later start cleans it).

docs.title: Tool-call safety evidence (2026-10-15, CLI 2.1.300)
docs.text:
What guarantees that nothing runs, and what is only defence in depth:

Barrier Kind Evidence No executable tool exists: --tools "" leaves only the stub's tools (init event lists exactly them) guarantee every run's init event The stub only lists tools; tools/call answers "not executed" guarantee code (about 20 lines); the CLI did reach it in some runs, with no effect A PreToolUse hook (via --settings) denies every call defence in depth without a sandbox: 0 stub calls in run-to-end mode, both attempts in permission_denials; it runs through a shell and fails open when it cannot start interrupt at the call boundary defence in depth, tidiness the call can still reach the stub in the window

--permission-prompts none does not block MCP tool calls. A permission deny rule or --disallowedTools hides the tool from the model, so neither can serve as a barrier.

Battery: 11 attacks (shell, file write, network, sub-agent, injection in a tool description, app tools named Bash/Write, transcript injection, web search, slash and ! commands, MCP self-configuration) on haiku and sonnet, each in the production configuration and with only the stub as barrier (no hook, no interrupt, run to the end), with harmless canary files as the target: - Unsandboxed, 26 runs: no canary, no call to a non-app tool, no web search, no file changed in the working folder or sandbox; production runs reached the stub 0 times. - Under a macOS sandbox-exec profile denying every program launch and file write outside an allow-list, 32 runs including a control call that must succeed: the CLI worked normally and nothing outside the allow-list was possible.

What the CLI itself starts on every request, tools or not: a copy of itself, git (hooks disabled; checks the empty working folder for .claude/settings.local.json), ps (its own start time), ioreg (machine id) and, on macOS, /usr/bin/security (its sign-in). It also updates .claude.json in the profile and keeps a session record with a local messaging socket while running.

  1. /v1/responses on Claude models: the same Claude runner behind a Responses translation (input items to the transcript, output as Responses objects and streamed events). Server-side tools (web search, file search) stay unsupported on Claude.
  2. Files on Claude models: file_id and inline files through the same structured input as images: images as image blocks, PDFs as document blocks (verified live 2026-10-15: a base64 PDF and a plain-text document block were both read and replayed as document blocks), text files inlined.
  3. Conversations on Claude models: the relay already stores the history, so conversation works as on GPT models (history prepended to the transcript).

docs.text: • Fake-CLI tests for every trap above; opt-in live tests with 8x8 images and a tool round trip; an adversarial audit; local redeploy before release.

docs.title: Outcome
docs.text:
• One Claude runner (stream-json in and out, one user message per run, non-streaming drains the same stream), airelay.claude_content for the transcript with media in place, airelay.media for the image and document check shared with the GPT path, airelay.chat_responses for /v1/responses and conversation items over the chat path, and airelay.claude_tool_stub / airelay.claude_tool_guard for tool calls.
  • Tool safety as recorded above, plus: tool runs require the stub's tools in the init report (502 cli_tools_unavailable otherwise), a call to any undefined tool stops the run, the stop at the call is bounded, and failures that say nothing about an account never pause one (NO_PAUSE_CODES).
  • strict: true tools run non-strict and are disclosed; forced calls, parallel_tool_calls: false and non-function tools are refused.
  • Follow-up: verify the PreToolUse hook command line on Windows (it fails open there if the CLI's hook shell rejects it; the stub stays the guarantee).

• Created: 2026-07-11

docs.title: Question investigated
docs.text: Can an OpenAI account's absolute 5h-window capacity (input/output tokens) be estimated from the relay's own usage history (per-request token accounting correlated with used_percent movement), and should the relay ship such an estimate?

docs.title: What the investigation established
docs.text:
• Window semantics (from live log evidence): the 5h window is a fixed bucket anchored at first use — reset_at freezes at first_use + 18000s, used_percent grows cumulatively, then hard-resets. Pairing snapshots with identical reset_at and differencing percent is therefore well-posed.
  • Empirical tokens-per-percent (Jul 11 logs, pairs with identical reset_at, Δpercent ≥ 2, censored at 100%):
  • plus account: median ≈ 22k tokens/percent → ≈ 2.2M tokens per 5h window, but cross-pair spread 316–651%
  • enterprise account: median ≈ 0.58–0.89M tokens/percent → ≈ 58–89M tokens per 5h window, spread 150–234%
  • a cached-discounted basis (cached input at 0.1 weight) consistently reduced spread, consistent with credit-weighted upstream metering
  • Why a shipped estimate was rejected:
  • The unit is wrong: the upstream quota is credit-denominated with per-model, per-token-class weights spanning ~400x (published Codex rate card), so "capacity in tokens" depends entirely on traffic mix — the observed spreads are structural, not sampling noise.
  • Integer percent quantization makes large plans nearly unobservable (~1 point per ~1M tokens → ±25–100% error for a long time).
  • Usage outside the relay (same subscription in first-party apps) biases estimates downward by an unknowable amount; window roll effects bias upward.
  • ADR 0001 forbids invented token budgets; a point estimate is exactly that, and even an honest range ("30–300M depending on mix") is practically useless.
  • Routing must not consume it: balanced routing's percent equalization is already the correct fixed point (it splits traffic proportionally to capacity without knowing it, and all accounts exhaust simultaneously); absolute-remaining routing would front-load the large account and behave worse under estimate error.
  • The wham/usage payload exposes no absolute quota anywhere (full field inventory checked), and public plan documentation covers neither the unit nor enterprise org policies.

docs.title: Sanctioned fallback (since shipped)
docs.text: The ground-truth reduced form shipped on 2026-07-12 as the Accounts card "more" hover: per-model input/output tokens served via the relay in the current 5h window plus totals (window_tokens on the account status payload; tallied in src/airelay/usage_tally.py). No extrapolation, no capacity claims — exactly the boundary this item drew.

docs.title: Original fallback description
docs.text: If capacity visibility is ever wanted in UI, the honest reduced form is the observed exchange rate composed purely of ground truth — e.g. "this 5h window: 1.9M tokens via relay ≈ 47 points" — with no extrapolation, no persistence, no routing coupling. If the upstream ever exposes credit-denominated usage (the payload's credits block shows the shape exists), read it instead of estimating.

• Done in 0.17.1: tauri-plugin-single-instance (a second launch focuses the running app's dashboard; verified on macOS with open -n and a direct binary launch) and the per-data-directory relay lock (data_dir/relay.lock, informational relay.pid, through private_io.InterProcessLock). A relay refused by the lock exits with status 75; the tray drops its intent to run, notifies once and does not restart it. Login-item launches pass --autostart, so a second instance started by the login item does not open the dashboard (existing login items are re-registered at startup).
  • To verify on Windows and Linux: one tray after a second launch and after a login-item launch, and the status-75 handling.
  • Remaining: everything else below (lifeline stdin, tray handling of a relay managed elsewhere, installer --quit, Linux tray detection, Windows port 1455, macOS PATH fallback, config rewrite).

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
• --lifeline-stdin (passed only by the tray): the relay reads stdin in a daemon thread and shuts down gracefully on EOF; SIGTERM takes the same path. Replace uvicorn.run with a Server whose should_exit the lifeline sets; graceful timeout about 3 s; the relay ends its own claude children. Services (systemd, launchd, Task Scheduler, nohup) give an empty stdin, so the flag must stay opt-in.
  • The tray signals only the relay; process-group SIGKILL (Unix) or the Job Object (Windows) remain backstops after at least 10 s. On Windows a tray crash still kills the relay at once (KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE); accepted.
  • data_dir/relay.lock: exclusive, non-blocking lock (msvcrt LK_NBLCK at a far offset on Windows; pid kept in a separate file, informational only). The tray reports "relay managed elsewhere (pid N)" instead of fighting it.
  • tauri-plugin-single-instance on all OSes, with a --quit path used by installers instead of force-killing.
  • Linux: detect org.kde.StatusNotifierWatcher before hiding the window (GNOME without AppIndicator has no tray); fix the autostart Exec quoting and the extract-and-run prefix; drop the stale libfuse2 check.
  • Windows: exclusive bind for the login callback port 1455 and a clear message for WinError 10013.
  • macOS: PATH discovery through an interactive login shell as a fallback only (markers, 10 s timeout, kill the process group); doctor reports a non-GUI session (launchctl managername, SSH variables, enrolled Claude profiles reporting signed out) without touching the keychain.
  • Wall-clock reset deadlines for benches and cooldowns (proposed item 0014).
  • The tray rewrites config.toml on every relay start and drops keys it does not model (for example [providers.claude].command). Edit only the keys the user changed (toml_edit), or model claude_command in the tray settings; until then desktop users set AIRELAYS_CLAUDE_COMMAND.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
• Lifecycle tests per OS: kill the tray, assert the relay exits (graceful on Unix, job kill on Windows); a second relay on the same data dir is refused.
  • systemd/launchd/Task Scheduler smoke: the relay keeps running with an empty stdin.

docs.title: Proposed: Wall-clock bench expiry across system sleep
Metadata
docs.text:
• Created: 2026-07-11
  • Status: Proposed

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Store the upstream-reported wall-clock reset time (reset_at epoch) alongside the monotonic bench deadline and expire a bench when either clock says the window has reset.

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: Bench deadlines use time.monotonic(), which does not advance during system sleep on macOS. A multi-hour bench on a laptop that sleeps overnight persists past the real window reset; until a usage probe or the launch warm-up corrects it, traffic keeps avoiding an account that actually has capacity.

docs.title: Current code reality
docs.text: _PooledAccount.limited_until and all bench arithmetic in src/airelay/accounts.py are monotonic-only. The upstream usage payload and 429 bodies carry absolute reset times (reset_at, resets_in_seconds) that are currently only converted to relative cooldowns. The launch warm-up (warm_start) already self-heals this after a restart, which reduces the severity.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
• add an optional wall-clock expiry to the bench state
  • treat "either clock says reset" as recovered
  • no persistence to disk (fresh probes remain the source of truth)

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: • unit test simulating a monotonic/wall divergence

docs.title: Proposed: Import OpenAI sign-ins saved in the OS keyring
Metadata
docs.text:
• Created: 2026-10-11
  • Status: Proposed (deferred by the owner)

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Offer a one-time, user-initiated import of OpenAI sign-ins that AIRelays 0.16.0 and earlier stored in the OS keyring, so upgraded users keep their accounts without signing in again.

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: ADR 0008 makes private files the only credential store. Sign-ins an older version kept in the keyring are reported by airelays doctor and need a new sign-in. The owner chose not to ship an import system for 0.16.1 to keep the product simple; a one-off script covered the owner's own migration.

docs.title: Constraints from the cross-OS review
docs.text:
• Reading the keyring can prompt (macOS ties items to the interpreter that last wrote them) or block (a locked Linux collection has no unlock timeout), so an import must run only on explicit user action, in a separate process with a hard timeout, never on the relay's event loop.
  • Linux: check is_locked() through Secret Service and skip a locked collection instead of prompting.
  • Only import roots without an auth.json; the file is always newer.
  • Windows has nothing to import (the keyring writes never succeeded).
  • Would re-add keyring as a dependency for the import window only.

docs.title: Promotion criteria
docs.text: Evidence that upgraded users lose accounts in practice and that signing in again is a real burden.

docs.title: Proposed: Claude token shape validation on set-token
Metadata
docs.text:
• Created: 2026-07-11
  • Status: Proposed

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Validate the pasted token's shape in airelays claude set-token (expected sk-ant-oat01- prefix, sane length floor) and warn on mismatch before storing.

docs.title: Reason
docs.text: claude setup-token prints the token once and line-wraps in narrow terminals; a copied first line still looks like a token and only fails later with a confusing upstream 401 at the first request. Catching a truncated paste at store time turns a delayed, hard-to-diagnose failure into an immediate, actionable message. There is a reported upstream issue for exactly this failure mode.

docs.title: Current code reality
docs.text: airelays claude set-token (src/airelay/cli.py) stores the pasted value as-is via Settings.write_claude_oauth_token. The usage path already fingerprints rejected tokens (src/airelay/providers.py) but only after an upstream 401.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
• prefix/length sanity check with a clear warning and a confirmation path for intentionally different tokens
  • strip embedded whitespace/newlines from pastes
  • no change to storage format or env fallback

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: • unit tests for accepted, truncated, and whitespace-wrapped pastes

docs.title: Proposed: Metered embeddings capability slice (single API key, embeddings only)
Metadata
docs.text:
• Created: 2026-07-13
  • Status: Proposed
  • Completed: N/A

docs.title: ADR status
docs.text:
• Governing ADRs: ADR 0002 (subscription backend compatibility boundary), ADR 0003 (default-deny relay security), ADR 0004 (provider runtime boundary)
  • ADR impact: Needs new ADR before promotion. ADR 0002 defines the product as subscription-backed, explicitly "not on a user-supplied OpenAI platform API key", and 0.2.3 deliberately removed the last API-key path. Implementing this item requires an ADR that amends or supersedes that scope with a narrow capability-complement rule (see Proposed direction). Do not implement from this backlog item alone.

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Vector embeddings are physically impossible through both enrolled subscription runtimes (verified live 2026-07-13):

  • The ChatGPT Codex backend has no embeddings route (an unauthenticated probe of /backend-api/codex/embeddings behaves exactly like a nonexistent path, unlike /responses → 401 and /models → 405), its model catalog carries no embedding models, and forcing an embedding model id onto /responses is rejected upstream: "The 'text-embedding-3-small' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account."
  • Anthropic has no first-party embedding models at all — their docs state "Anthropic does not offer its own embedding model" and recommend Voyage AI; api.anthropic.com/v1/embeddings is a genuine 404. The claude CLI surface is text generation only.

So today no client of AIRelays can obtain embeddings, and the relay's /v1/embeddings route answers an honest 501. An adversarial design review (2026-07-13, Fable 5) of a broader proposal — general API-key providers for OpenAI/Anthropic/OpenRouter/OVH — rejected the broad version (identity conflict with ADR 0002, security model sized for quota not dollars, "passthrough" collapsing into a translation layer by the third provider) but explicitly kept alive this minimal slice: one metered credential, one capability, namespaced and opt-in.

docs.title: Current code reality
docs.text:
Inspected 2026-07-13:

  • src/airelay/app.py: /v1/embeddings is registered in the unsupported_route group and returns 501 unsupported_error before any upstream contact.
  • src/airelay/providers.py: provider-scoped runtimes with namespaced model ids (claude:*) and per-model route capability metadata published via /v1/models — the structural pattern this slice would follow.
  • src/airelay/auth.py: AuthStorage (keyring-backed) is the correct home for a metered key. The desktop rewrites config.toml (accounts.py docstring), so the key must never live there.
  • src/airelay/config.py: validate_provider_guardrails() is the precedent for a hard startup interlock (Claude refuses non-loopback listeners); the metered key needs an equivalent (refuse to start with a key configured in --no-auth mode).
  • src/airelay/security.py: one shared relay bearer token, request-denominated rate limits — no per-client scoping or spend controls exist.
  • src/airelay/traffic.py: logs full JSON request/response bodies; raw embedding vectors (thousands of floats per response) would bloat hourly logs and the desktop traffic reader, so vector payloads must be summarized, never logged raw.
  • src/airelay/accounts.py: the pool retries on 429/5xx — free on subscriptions, a spend multiplier on metered calls; the metered path must not inherit retries.

docs.title: Problem or opportunity
docs.text:
Two candidate benefits, both uncertain:

  1. Capability: RAG-style workloads next to chat need embeddings; the relay cannot serve them and forces a second endpoint into every client config.
  2. Key custody: apps would hold only the relay token while the real billing key lives in one place (keyring), with one rotation point and unified traffic logging across subscription and metered usage.

Honest counter-position (owner's own doubt, recorded deliberately): this may be useless in practice. Any app can point its embeddings base URL directly at OpenAI (same API shape, upstream-enforceable project budgets) or at a local model. The marginal value may reduce to key-management centralization alone — and centralizing a billing key behind one shared, unscoped bearer token is a richer theft target as much as it is a convenience. That trade cuts both ways and is the core reason this item is proposed, not planned.

docs.title: Proposed direction
docs.text:
A capability-complement rule, to be codified in the new ADR: metered credentials may exist only for capabilities no enrolled subscription can physically provide — today, exactly embeddings.

  • Serve /v1/embeddings only for explicitly namespaced ids (e.g. openai-api:text-embedding-3-small); bare or subscription model ids keep the current rejection; every other 501 route stays 501.
  • Opt-in, off by default; key stored via AuthStorage (keyring), never config.toml.
  • Hard interlock: refuse to start when a metered key is configured together with --no-auth (open mode), mirroring validate_provider_guardrails().
  • No retries/failover on the metered path.
  • Traffic logs record dims/bytes/hash summaries of vectors, never raw payloads.
  • Desktop: one plain "Embeddings" line (request and token counts, link to the upstream billing dashboard, explicit "AIRelays does not enforce spend caps" note). No usage bars, no windows, no pretending.
  • Setup docs require an endpoint-restricted, budget-capped OpenAI project key so a stolen key is nearly worthless.

docs.title: Why it might matter
docs.text:
• Closes the only verified capability hole in the OpenAI-compatible surface while keeping the subscription identity intact (one narrow, explicitly bounded exception instead of a general metered gateway).
  • Preserves the "one endpoint, one client secret" story for mixed chat+RAG apps.
  • The bounded shape is cheap to hold: embeddings is the most stable OpenAI route — no streaming, no tools, spend measured in cents per million tokens.

docs.title: Promotion criteria
docs.text:
Promote to planned/ only when all of these hold:

  1. A concrete, recurring need is demonstrated (a real workflow that wants chat and embeddings through the same relay endpoint — not a hypothetical).
  2. The competing alternatives are reassessed and rejected for that need: local embeddings via an ollama:*-style adapter (no key, no billing, follows the claude CLI precedent), direct provider config in the client app, or a documented sidecar (e.g. LiteLLM) holding keys with AIRelays as one upstream.
  3. The superseding/amending ADR is drafted and accepted (capability-complement rule, non-goals, and the open-mode interlock as policy).
  4. The owner accepts the custody trade-off explicitly: billing key behind one shared bearer token, no per-client scopes, no relay-side spend enforcement.

docs.title: Validation ideas
docs.text:
• Unit: namespaced id routing, rejection of bare/subscription ids on /v1/embeddings, startup interlock with --no-auth, key resolution from keyring only.
  • Traffic: assert vector payloads are summarized (dims/bytes/hash) in logs.
  • Live: one real embeddings call through the relay against a budget-capped project key; confirm token counts surface in the desktop line.
  • Docs: FAQ entry explaining why embeddings are impossible via subscriptions and when to prefer direct/local/sidecar alternatives instead of this slice.

docs.title: Non-goals
docs.text:
This proposal does not authorize:

  • metered chat/completions/responses of any kind;
  • OpenRouter, Anthropic API, or OVH providers (OpenRouter does not reliably close the embeddings gap and aggregation is better consumed directly);
  • any subscription→metered fallback, silent or configured;
  • images/audio/realtime unlocks;
  • spend dashboards or relay-side budget enforcement (v1 explicitly displays "no spend caps" instead);
  • per-client scoped relay tokens (a prerequisite for any broader centralization ambition, tracked separately if that product bet is ever made).

docs.title: Guidance for future agents
docs.text: Re-verify the capability gap before acting: if either subscription upstream gains an embeddings surface, or if a local-embeddings adapter lands first, this item likely dies — check deprecated/ fit before promoting. Read ADR 0002 and the 0.2.3 changelog entry first; the identity boundary is deliberate and this item is an exception to it, not a precedent for general API-key support. If the real underlying need turns out to be "centralize all my keys", stop and write that up as its own decision (per-client scoped tokens and budgets as the entry fee) rather than stretching this slice.
